screening_results.reason: Although this is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity with an Alcohol>Water contrast and reports participant/sample details, it does not meet key inclusion requirements for this meta-analysis. The task used taste cues (oral alcohol delivery) with only brief visual word prompts rather than a visual cue-reactivity paradigm, so it does not satisfy the requirement for cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3). Critically, the reported analyses are ROI-based (ventral striatum) and the paper does not provide or rely on a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map to support the reported effects; the authors note that whole-brain analyses did not elicit significant mesocorticolimbic clusters. Therefore it falls under exclusion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain activation map). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures) in cocaine-dependent individuals. It reports a within-subject contrast (cocaine > neutral) with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE-corrected and cluster-level results), and provides demographic/sex information, cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The article describes development and validation of an image database and selection of image sets and Psychopy code for fMRI tasks, but it does not report any human fMRI data, task-evoked whole-brain analyses, or within-participant contrasts of drug cues>control. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI study), I4 (within-participant contrast drug>control), I5/I6 (whole-brain task activation maps). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study is an fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual drug (cocaine) and neutral videos (satisfying I3), the provided full text reports only subjective craving outcomes and does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or activation contrasts (drug>control). No voxelwise results, coordinate tables, figures, or whole-brain analyses are described. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task activation evidence (I5/I4). As such, it should be excluded under the review exclusion criteria for studies lacking whole-brain results.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes a within-participant contrast (cocaine > neutral images), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-test and between-group and regression analyses) with SPM8 and cluster-level correction, and presents results in tables/figures with coordinates. Relevant participant and methodological details are reported (sex distribution, cue type: cocaine, scanner field strength: 3.0T, processing software: SPM8; age is referenced in Table 1). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task map, or non-empirical) are violated. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (and reports whole-brain analyses for regulation contrasts), the paper does not present a within-participant drug-cue>control (e.g., alcohol>neutral or alcohol>food) whole-brain group-level task activation map required for cue-reactivity meta-analysis. Reported whole-brain contrasts focus on regulation (LATER>NOW; REAPPRAISE>LOOK) and parametric modulation by craving, not a direct cue-reactivity contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 and the required cue-reactivity whole-brain evidence (I5). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cannabis cues in adolescents and reports within-subject contrasts (cannabis > non-cannabis). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (FLAME; cluster-corrected Z thresholds) and results are reported across whole-brain clusters. Key methodological details required by the review (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, processing software FSL) are provided. The study does not violate any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes an unmasked whole-brain task effect). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation using visual heroin-related cues versus neutral images in heroin-maintained patients and healthy controls. It reports within-subject contrasts (BOLD drug cues > BOLD neutral) and group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (with FWE-corrected clusters reported), and also provides details on participant age/sex, cue type (heroin), scanner (3T), and processing software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7.

The paper contains a pilot fMRI study using visual alcohol vs neutral cues with a within-participant alcohol>neutral contrast and reports whole-brain group-level results, but it does not explicitly report MRI scanner field strength or the processing software in the provided full text. Inclusion criterion I7 requires reporting of participant age and sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software; scanner field strength and processing software are not available in the accessible text (they are referred to in Supplementary Information, which is not provided). Therefore at least one required inclusion criterion (I7) is not satisfied, so the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the core inclusion requirement I3: it is a PET study ([18F]fallypride) measuring dopamine release, not an fMRI study. It therefore does not provide task-evoked whole-brain fMRI activation maps (I5) required for the meta-analysis. Although the study uses within-subject cue versus neutral contrasts (similar in design to I4) and reports ROI-based analyses of cue effects, it reports ROI PET binding results with no whole-brain voxelwise fMRI task maps. The full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus it is ineligible for inclusion in an fMRI-based cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (cocaine vs neutral pictures) in recently abstinent cocaine-dependent participants. It includes a within-participant contrast (cocaine > neutral) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (one-sample t tests for the cocaine>neutral contrast, with voxel- and cluster-level corrected results and supplementary tables). Relevant methodological details are reported (participant age and sex, cue type: cocaine, scanner: 3T, software: SPM8). The paper also reports additional connectivity analyses but does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity results. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

The study used gustatory (taste) alcohol cues (alcohol vs. juice tastes) rather than visual stimuli. The meta-analysis requires cue-reactivity studies that use visual stimuli (I3). Although the study does include a within-participant alcohol>control contrast (alcohol>juice), reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps, and provides participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software, it fails to meet the essential visual-stimulus inclusion criterion. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual drug-related stimuli (alcohol- and cannabis-related words). Participants performed an addiction-Stroop task with within-subject contrasts (alcohol > neutral color, cannabis > neutral color) and first-level contrasts were carried to group-level random-effects analyses. The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using SPM8 with cluster-level correction and report significant clusters and brain–behavior correlations (i.e., qualifying whole-brain results described in text/tables/figures). Key participant demographic details (age/sex counts), cue types (alcohol, cannabis), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This study examined nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli and within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts, but the cue-reactivity results are reported using a priori ROIs (four insula subregions and two ACC ROIs) and subsequent ROI-based beta extractions and regressions. No group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or whole-brain task results are reported in the provided full text; task analyses focus on ROI beta weights and resting-state connectivity. Therefore it qualifies as an ROI-only task analysis and meets exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI visual drug cue reactivity) and I4 (within-participant drug>control contrast) but I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map) is not met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of tobacco (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures) in smokers and matched non-smokers. The design includes within-participant contrasts of craving (Cr) and aversion (Av) pictures versus control mosaic scenes, and group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses with voxelwise inference (FDR thresholds reported). Results are reported as whole-brain activations (regions/BA, p-values) and correlations with behavioral measures. The manuscript reports participant sex (male), describes age-matched groups, cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cocaine-cue videotapes to elicit craving. It includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., emotion 0 vs baseline 1, emotion 1 vs emotion 0, emotion 2 vs baseline 2) that directly assess responses to drug cues versus control/baseline stimuli. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (randomization procedure across voxels; results presented as maps and region listings), with figures/tables of activations reported. Participant age and sex, cue type (cocaine), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM 96) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures). The design includes within-participant contrasts of food vs. control pictures and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (with ROI and whole-brain results, coordinates and figures). Participant age and sex, MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study examines nicotine cue-reactivity with visual smoking images and reports within-subject contrasts (smoke > rest) and detailed participant/scanner/procedural information. However, the reported analyses and results focus on individualized ROI-based percent signal change and subjective measures; the paper does not present or describe a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results).

This article is a narrative/synthesis paper summarizing results from a series of ERP and fMRI studies rather than reporting an original, single empirical fMRI study with primary whole-brain task activation maps. The full text does not present methods, participant details, scanner field strength, or group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) drug>control contrast maps or coordinates that could be extracted. Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion requirements (I3–I7) and fits exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical/review without original human fMRI data).

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol and cannabis marketing cues and neutral control stimuli, with within-participant contrasts (drug-marketing > neutral) and group-level whole-brain GLM analyses. The manuscript provides participant age/sex, cue types (alcohol, cannabis), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (SPM8). Whole-brain results are described in the text and supported by figures/tables; ROI analyses are reported but whole-brain task-evoked maps and cluster results are also presented. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that examines neural responses to visual anticipatory cues predicting monetary reward and loss (natural reward-related cues) using the monetary incentive delay (MID) task. It includes within-subject contrasts (Reward Cue–Neutral Cue and Loss Cue–Neutral Cue), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME whole-brain results reported and thresholded, with tables/figures), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (monetary), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a visual alcohol cue reactivity task in treatment-seeking alcohol-dependent participants. The manuscript reports within-participant contrasts (Alcohol > Control) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM12) with cluster-level FWE correction and MNI coordinates for significant clusters. Relevant methodological details are provided (3T scanner field strength, preprocessing and statistical analysis in SPM12) and participant demographics (age, sex) and cue type (alcohol visual stimuli) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3 (fMRI visual cue-reactivity), I4 (within-participant drug cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), I6 (coordinates and figures reported), and I7 (age/sex, cue type, scanner, software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual heroin cue videos and within-participant drug cue > neutral contrasts, but the reported analyses are ROI-based time-course and correlational analyses. The manuscript does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps, coordinate tables, or whole-brain results in the text or figures. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-subject contrasts (Smoking > Neutral) and conducts whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FLAME) with cluster correction (z=3.1, Pcorrected < .05). Relevant methodological details required by the meta-analysis are provided: participant age range, sex/gender matching, cue type (nicotine), MRI scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (FSL). Results include one-sample (within-group) and between-group whole-brain maps and tables/figures describing activated clusters and coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes unmasked task effects). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (videos) to elicit cocaine- and gambling-related cue reactivity. Within-subject contrasts were performed (V1>B1 and V2>B2 for each video type), and group-level, whole-brain random-effects ANOVAs were reported with family-wise-error correction and tables/figures of peak coordinates. The paper reports participant ages and sex breakdown, cue types (cocaine, gambling, sad), MRI scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (SPM5, AFNI, BioImage Suite). Thus it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity with visual stimuli and provides whole-brain task-evoked results and necessary methodological/demographic details.

This is an fMRI study using visual cues (drug and food videos) to assess cue-reactivity in cocaine-dependent and control participants. It reports within-participant contrasts (DRUG vs FOOD), group-level whole-brain task analyses (flexible factorial Group x VideoType interaction) with cluster coordinates and ROI small-volume corrections, and provides participant age/sex, cue types (cocaine, food), scanner field strength (3T Siemens TrioTim), and processing software (SPM12). Thus it meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI cue-reactivity with visual stimuli, provides a within-subject contrast of cue types, reports whole-brain group-level results (tables/coordinates/supplement), and includes required participant and acquisition details.

Although this is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli with a within-subject alcohol vs neutral contrast (I3, I4) and reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software (I7), the paper’s primary results are ROI-to-ROI gPPI connectivity analyses. The report does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain voxelwise activation results (only ROI-based connectivity findings). This violates the requirement for a whole-brain task activation analysis (I5). Therefore the study must be excluded under exclusion criterion E4 (connectivity-only analyses without whole-brain task maps). Full text appears complete.

The study used auditory guided-imagery (personalized audiotaped scripts) rather than visual cue stimuli. The meta-analysis specifically requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3). Although the study includes within-participant contrasts (favorite-food vs neutral), whole-brain group-level analyses, and reports relevant participant and MRI details, it does not meet I3 and therefore does not qualify for inclusion.

Full text is truncated/behind paywall (methods, results, and figures are partially inaccessible) so the full report is incomplete. From available content, this JoVE protocol reports rtfMRI neurofeedback in 4 nicotine-dependent smokers focusing on downregulation of bilateral insula in response to craving cues. The paper appears to emphasize ROI neurofeedback training (insula) with a very small sample and does not present or describe a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast in the accessible text. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps (I5) or clear within-participant cue>control contrasts reported at whole-brain level (I4). Given the incomplete full text and likely ROI-focused analyses, the study should be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine) in adolescents. The study reports within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > neutral cues and conducts second-level, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (thresholds and cluster criteria reported). Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol > neutral) during a validated cue-reactivity task and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2×2 factorial and one-sample/two-sample t tests) with family-wise-error correction procedures and cluster thresholds. Processing software (SPM8/SPM12) and MRI scanner field strength (3 T) are explicitly described; participant age range and sex (male-only) and cue type (alcohol) are reported. Whole-brain results are described in the text and tables/figures; ROI analyses are supplementary but do not replace whole-brain reporting. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue paradigms (pictures) for drug (cocaine) and natural reward (food) cues, reporting within-participant contrasts (cocaine vs neutral; food vs neutral). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster- and voxel-level thresholds reported) and presents cluster results and figures; processing software (SPM) and participant demographics (age, sex, BMI) are provided. MRI protocol is described in the Supplement (acceptable per inclusion rules). Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study does not meet inclusion criterion I3 because cue exposure was delivered via individualized audiotaped imagery scripts (auditory/imagery paradigm), not visual stimuli. Although it satisfies several other requirements (within-participant contrasts of favorite-food vs neutral (I4); group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction reported (I5/I6); and provides participant demographics, cue type (food), scanner field strength, and software details (I7)), the meta-analysis specifically requires visual cue-reactivity paradigms. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual food cue-reactivity (natural reward). It reports within-subject contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie foods), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests and multiple regression), and reports coordinates and cluster results. Necessary methodological details are provided (participant age and sex: females 18–35; cue type: food; MRI field strength: 3T; processing software: SPM12/MATLAB). Results include whole-brain activations and small-volume corrected amygdala findings, satisfying reporting requirements. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion and conclusions. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an empirical BOLD fMRI investigation of visual smoking (nicotine) cues using a within-subject cue-reactivity task (smoking-related images vs. neutral images). The authors report within-participant contrasts (smoking cue > neutral) and conduct group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster- and familywise-error correction, presenting significant clusters and extracted percent signal change. The manuscript reports participant age and sex distribution, cue type (nicotine), MRI scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images). The authors computed within-participant contrasts comparing trials containing a smoking image versus two neutral images (beta maps), used these in MVPA, and performed group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (accuracy maps warped to MNI space and tested with cluster correction), reporting significant clusters/coordinates and describing results in the text. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and software (SPM8, AFNI, FSL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The abstract and available content indicate an fMRI cue-reactivity study using alcohol-related visual stimuli (I3) and that a within-subject contrast (alcohol vs neutral) was performed (I4), but the simple contrast was reported as non-significant and the authors emphasize psychophysiological interaction (seed-based PPI) connectivity results. The provided full text is paywalled/incomplete, and there is no clear report of a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map in the accessible content. Therefore I5 (whole-brain task activation evidence) is not met and the study appears to report only seed-based connectivity analyses without whole-brain task maps, meeting exclusion E4. Full text is incomplete/unavailable, preventing verification of whole-brain results.

This study is an fMRI investigation of cannabis cue-reactivity using visual/tactile cues and reports seed-based PPI (functional connectivity) and Granger (effective connectivity) results comparing cannabis vs neutral cues. However, the paper does not report a univariate, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map for drug cues > control stimuli (only seed-based connectivity/effective connectivity results are presented). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only seed-based/effective connectivity without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual alcohol cues (alcohol vs nonalcohol beverage images) and reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol to control stimuli (e.g., CRAlcohol - CRControl, GOAlcohol - GOControl). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (family-wise error corrected results presented in tables and figures). Participant age and sex are provided, cue type is alcohol, scanner field strength (3.0 T) and processing software (SPM8) are specified. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (images) in heavy-drinking participants, directly addressing cue-reactivity. It includes within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues > rest/control (contrast alcohol cues > rest used across blocks) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (e.g., whole-brain FWE-corrected activation in right inferior frontal gyrus for feedback>rest; coordinates reported for peaks). Relevant participant demographics (age, sex distribution), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Results are reported with peak coordinates and statistical thresholds. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study examines fMRI cue-reactivity to visual food cues (natural reward) and includes within-subject food>neutral contrasts and reports participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, analyses are conducted using a priori ROI masks (AAL) and report ROI-based results; the paper does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). The full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The experiment uses within-subject contrasts that map appetitive cues vs control (e.g., ADMIT_TASTY > ADMIT_NOT_TASTY and ADMIT_TASTY > REGULATE_TASTY). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level maps are reported (voxelwise threshold P<0.001, cluster-level FWE correction for the whole brain). Methods report scanner field strength (3 T) and processing software (SPM8), and participant sex and age covariates are described. Therefore the study satisfies I3–I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Although this is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts (alcoholic > non-alcoholic) with coordinates and relevant participant/scanner information (satisfying I3, I4, I6, I7), the second-level/group analyses were spatially restricted to an anatomically defined mesocorticolimbic mask rather than being reported as an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map. Therefore the study does not meet I5 (whole-brain evidence) and must be excluded from the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete.

The study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual cues as required. It uses a monetary incentive delay task (monetary reward anticipation vs verbal feedback) to index reward sensitivity, not a cue-reactivity paradigm contrasting drug or natural reward cues versus control stimuli. Therefore criteria I3 and I4 are not met. The paper does report group-level whole-brain task activation results and provides relevant methodological details (scanner field strength, processing software, participant age/sex), so I5, I6 and I7 are satisfied, but failing I3/I4 mandates exclusion. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI within-subject study using the Monetary Incentive Delay task with visual reward cues (reward vs neutral) — i.e., natural reward-related cue-reactivity. The study reports within-participant contrasts of reward>neutral (anticipation and outcome), group-level voxelwise analyses (FLAME mixed-effects; whole-brain cluster correction applied for several contrasts including PPI results) and reports coordinates/figures. Participant age and sex, cue type (monetary reward), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are provided. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without task activation, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

Although this is an fMRI study of visual cannabis cue-reactivity with a within-participant cannabis>neutral contrast and reports participant demographics and scanner/software (satisfying I3, I4, I7), the reported analyses are ROI-based (mean % signal change extracted from anatomically defined ROIs) and the follow-up analyses appear restricted to ROI masks. The paper does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the cannabis>neutral contrast; the voxelwise follow-up analysis described was conducted within predefined ROIs (i.e., an exploratory ROI-localization using FLAME), and therefore qualifies as ROI-restricted reporting. Because no whole-brain, unmasked group-level task activation map is clearly reported, the study fails the whole-brain evidence inclusion requirement (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete.

Full text appears to be limited to abstract/metadata (fulltext_incomplete=true). Based on available information, the study uses a monetary incentive delay task with visual cues predicting monetary gain or loss avoidance rather than presenting drug-related or primary natural reward cues (e.g., food, sexual) or drug cues. Therefore it does not meet key inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues > control or natural reward-related cues > control), because the cues are monetary (conditioned/secondary reward) and not the target cue types for this meta-analysis. Whole-brain reporting appears likely (coordinates/voxelwise results described), but failure to satisfy I3/I4 is sufficient for exclusion. Confidence is moderate due to incomplete full text.

This study reports an empirical fMRI experiment using visual alcohol-associated cues in abstinent alcoholics and controls. It includes a within-participant contrast comparing alcohol-associated versus abstract/control stimuli, and reports group-level, voxelwise analyses conducted with SPM99 (fixed-effects group analysis) and whole-brain BOLD results (regions activated are described). Relevant participant information (ages, sex distribution), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM99) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods (psychophysiology and fMRI acquisition/analysis), results, and discussion, so the core article content is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without an unmasked task effect, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the paper satisfies all required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues with an explicit within-subject contrast (Alcohol>Neutral) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses. The paper reports whole-brain results (both ROI-corrected and exploratory whole-brain mappings) and provides coordinates/figures, fulfilling the requirement that whole-brain task-evoked maps are available. Necessary methodological details are reported (cue type: alcohol visual stimuli; scanner field strength: 3T; processing software: SPM8), and participant demographics and sex matching are described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues with within-subject contrasts (drug > neutral), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8, AlphaSim correction) and reported relevant participant and scanning information (male participants, matched by age, heroin cue type, 3.0T scanner, SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

Although this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of cannabis using visual stimuli with a within-subject cannabis cue > appetitive cue contrast and reports participant demographics and scanner/software details, the paper reports ROI-based analyses (mean z-statistics extracted from a priori anatomical masks) and does not present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinate tables/figures for whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only reporting).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, with within-subject contrasts comparing food>non-food, and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (whole-brain FWE-corrected activations reported). Methods report scanner field strength (3T), processing software (SPM12), and participant age/sex. Imaging data are available online (NeuroVault) and results include voxelwise analyses and coordinate reporting. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI study using visual cigarette-related and pleasant (natural reward) cues and reports within-subject contrasts (cigarette/pleasant > neutral) and a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM (FDR-thresholded). Participant age and sex and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. However, the provided full text does not report the MRI scanner field strength, which is required by inclusion criterion I7. Because I7 (reporting scanner field strength along with age/sex, cue type, and processing software) is not satisfied, the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual stimuli (e-cigarette and neutral videos) to assess cue-reactivity in experienced e-cigarette users. The analyses include within-participant contrasts of e-cigarette vs neutral videos (video condition main effect and session x video interaction) at the group level using a voxelwise repeated-measures ANOVA with cluster-level correction; whole-brain results are reported (including Talairach coordinates). The manuscript reports participant age range and demographic details, cue type (nicotine/e-cigarette), scanner field strength (3T Siemens), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an fMRI cue–reactivity study using visual cannabis cues (meets I3), the analysis is ROI-based and the authors explicitly state that “A voxelwise approach was not completed for this analysis.” No group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps are reported. Therefore the study does not meet the requirement for whole-brain results (I5) and falls under exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study examines monetary (non-drug) reward anticipation using symbolic arrow cues rather than visual drug-related or natural reward cues (e.g., alcohol images, food, sexual stimuli). Although it reports whole-brain voxelwise task effects and provides scanner/software/participant details, it does not assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity as required (fails I3 and I4). Therefore it does not meet the review’s key inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

The study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual stimuli (cocaine-related pictures vs natural scenes) and includes within-participant contrasts of cocaine>control stimuli. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (FSL GLM, Randomise, whole-brain thresholding), with results described in text and figures/tables. Participant demographics (male, mean age 56.5), cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength (3T Siemens), and processing software (FSL) are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling assessment. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment using visual stimuli (novel geometric cues) that were experimentally paired with alcohol intoxication and tests cue-reactivity (CS+ vs CS−). It includes a within-participant contrast of alcohol-paired cues > control cues ([CS+ > CS−]) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-level FWE correction; coordinates and tables/figures provided). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (cocaine, sexual, aversive, neutral) and reports within-subject contrasts (cocaine > neutral) across participants. The paper conducted group-level, voxelwise analyses (2×3 ANOVA and t-tests) with cluster-corrected whole-brain results (stated and reported in Table 2 and figures), and also presents coordinates/figures of activation. Participant demographics (mean age, sex distribution), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/analysis software (SPM8, AFNI, FSL) are reported. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This study is ineligible for the meta-analysis because it is a PET ([15O]H2O) imaging study using script-guided auditory mental imagery to induce craving, not an fMRI study using visual cues. Inclusion criterion I3 requires a functional MRI study with visual stimuli; this study uses PET and auditory imagery, so it fails I3 (modality) and the review’s cue-type requirement (visual stimuli). Although it reports within-participant contrasts (drug cues > neutral) and whole-brain voxelwise analyses with SPM, the imaging modality and cue modality do not match the meta-analysis objective, therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cannabis cue reactivity using visual stimuli (images of cannabis, cigarettes, neutral, and animals). It includes within-subject contrasts (Can > Neutral and Can > Neutral + Cigarette). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (FEAT, 2×2 ANOVA with random effects) and provides cluster results with peak MNI coordinates. Participant age/sex, cue type (cannabis/cigarette), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (fMRIPrep, FSL) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task map, or non-empirical) are violated. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward stimuli (infant faces/baby schema) in opioid use disorder patients, with within-subject contrasts (Low/Unmanipulated/High baby schema vs crosshair and High vs Low), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded and cluster-corrected) reported. Participant age/sex, cue type (infant faces), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining visual food cue reactivity (food vs nonfood images) within participants. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests and whole-brain multiple regression) with coordinates and thresholds, describes methods (SPM12), scanner (3T), and participant demographics (age, sex). It includes a within-participant contrast (food > nonfood), reports whole-brain results in text/tables/figures, and provides cue type (food). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual alcohol-related word cues (visual stimuli) and neutral word controls. The analysis includes within-participant contrasts of alcohol>neutral (fit coefficients contrasting conditions) and group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical tests (independent-samples t tests and single-sample t tests performed for each voxel, with AFNI and cluster correction reported). Participant age and sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner parameters and processing software (AFNI) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of cocaine cue reactivity using visual (and auditory) stimuli and within-subject contrasts; however, it does not report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps. The authors preselected ten neuroanatomic regions and report region-based activation measures (ROI-based analyses) rather than unmasked whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables. Therefore it violates the requirement for whole-brain evidence and meets the exclusion criterion for ROI-only studies. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation with within-subject Alcohol>Water contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise analyses reporting coordinates and necessary sample/scanner details. However, the cue modality is gustatory (alcohol taste delivered in scanner) rather than visual stimuli, so it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criterion requiring visual stimuli (I3). Therefore it must be excluded. All core article sections (intro, methods, results, discussion) are present, so full text is complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject CUE>neutral contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (FSL FLAME1) and whole-brain corrected results are reported (figures/tables). Relevant participant demographics, cue type, scanner (3T), and processing software (FSL) are provided. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity that included visual stimuli (grayscaled images) and reported within-participant contrasts of smoking cues vs control (e.g., VS–VC) as part of whole-brain, group-level RFX-GLM analyses. Whole-brain statistical maps were computed, corrected for multiple comparisons, and results are reported with cluster thresholds and coordinate tables/figures. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3 T), and analysis software (BrainVoyager) are all reported. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical human fMRI study using visual stimuli (three films including cocaine cues) in cocaine users and controls. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (one-sample and two-sample t tests with voxel-wise thresholds and cluster criteria) and provides cluster coordinates/tables and figures. Within-participant contrasts are present (cocaine film vs nature film in cocaine users), and additional between-group and between-film comparisons are reported. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (AFNI) are explicitly reported. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for whole-brain fMRI cue-reactivity with visual stimuli.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual heroin-related versus neutral stimuli in 14 male participants on methadone maintenance. The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing heroin-related > neutral cues and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (maps and tables; p < .0001, cluster-level corrected). Relevant metadata are provided: participant age/sex, cue type (heroin), 3-T scanner field strength, and processing software (SPM5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are violated.

This study is an fMRI investigation of nicotine (smoking)-related cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes a within-participant contrast (smoking-related > neutral images) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM) with corrected thresholds and cluster coordinates in tables. Key participant details (mean age, sex = women), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cue images and matched non-alcohol beverage images, reporting within-participant contrasts (alcohol > non-alcohol) and longitudinal behavioral outcomes. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted in AFNI with Monte Carlo cluster correction; significant clusters and Talairach coordinates are reported. The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5 preprocessing, AFNI group analysis). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with within-participant contrast (alcohol>neutral). It reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-test and multiple regression) with cluster correction and provides results in tables/figures. Participant demographics (age range, sex distribution), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM) are reported. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The provided full-text content is incomplete (page failed to load) and contains no Methods or Results. The title/metadata indicate a pharmacological study of varenicline and bupropion SR effects on craving/withdrawal, with no indication it is an fMRI study. Therefore it fails to meet key inclusion criterion I3 (functional MRI study using visual cue-reactivity). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot verify I4–I7 (within-participant drug>control contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise maps, reporting of participant and MRI details). Exclusion is based on failure to meet required inclusion criteria and incomplete full text preventing assessment.

This study is a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual alcohol cues (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage images) with a within-participant contrast (alcoholic cues > non-alcoholic cues). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were conducted (one-sample t-test, voxel-level thresholds reported) with coordinates and region-level results provided. Key methodological details required by the review are reported: participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of drug cue-reactivity that includes a visual cigarette cue paradigm (first-person video cues) and reports within-subject contrasts (Cigarette Cues > Control and Alcohol Cues > Control). Whole-brain GLMs were run (FEAT/FSL), peak precuneus coordinates are reported in MNI space, and group-level voxelwise analyses were performed to define ROIs via a leave-one-out whole-brain approach. Participant age/sex, cue types (nicotine and alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The cigarette cue component uses visual stimuli, satisfying the visual-stimuli requirement. Results (including coordinates) are reported and meet the meta-analysis reporting requirements. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videotaped cues). The paper reports within-subject contrasts including cigarette cues > neutral (cigarette cue crave vs neutral and cigarette cue resist vs neutral, and direct contrasts between cue conditions). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses were performed using FSL/FEAT with cluster correction (Z>2.3, p=0.01) and results are described in the text (with coordinate-based clusters), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an empirical perfusion fMRI (ASL) investigation of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using audio-visual/visual smoking stimuli. It reports a within-subject contrast of smoking cues > nonsmoking cues, uses voxel-wise, group-level random-effects SPM analyses (whole-brain maps with cluster results and coordinate tables/figures), and provides participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM2). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (shapes) in a monetary incentive delay task assessing neural responses to natural reward-related cues (money). It includes within-subject contrasts of reward cues > nonincentive cues and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-corrected maps and peak coordinates. Participant demographics, cue type (monetary), 3T scanner field strength, and processing software (AFNI) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This is an fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (cocaine videos) and an appetitive visual control (food videos), with within-subject contrasts separating cocaine versus food cue responses (hierarchical regression isolating cocaine>food variance). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses are reported (whole-brain contrasts, cluster thresholds, and stereotaxic coordinates/BA results described). Relevant methodological details are provided: cue types (cocaine and food), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (AFNI); participants are described as gender- and age-matched (participant counts provided). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues and neutral control images, reporting within-participant (heroin > neutral) contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with thresholding and cluster reporting. Participant demographics (male, age range 18–55), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (1.5 T Philips), and processing software are reported. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual drug-cue reactivity.

The provided “full text” consists only of the References section and article metadata (title, authors, journal, date, DOI). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is missing, so I cannot verify key inclusion criteria: whether the study used visual drug-related cues, reported a within-participant drug-cue>control contrast, or reported group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps (or coordinate tables). Because essential information is absent, the record cannot be assessed for eligibility for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation but uses personalized guided auditory imagery (favorite-food, stress, neutral-relaxing) rather than visual stimuli, so it does not meet the review’s requirement for cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (fails I3). The analyses focus on intrinsic connectivity distribution (ICD) and seed-to-voxel functional connectivity with between-group comparisons (smokers vs nonsmokers) rather than within-participant task-evoked contrasts of cue>control or presenting unmasked, whole-brain task activation maps; thus it does not satisfy I4 or I5. In addition, the reported results are connectivity-based (post hoc seed analyses) rather than task-evoked whole-brain activation maps, meeting exclusion criteria for connectivity-only studies (E4) and for reporting only between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain task effect (E5). Full text appears complete.

The study uses personalized audio-guided imagery (auditory cues) of favorite foods rather than visual stimuli. Inclusion criterion I3 requires cue-reactivity assessed using visual stimuli; this study therefore does not meet I3. The study does include within-participant contrasts of favorite-food cue > control and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results and participant/cue/scanner details, so I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on failure to meet the modality requirement (visual stimuli).

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual drug-related and pleasant images and measured cue-evoked BOLD responses. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of CSD+ versus CS− and CSP+ versus CS− (drug and natural/pleasant cues vs control), performed random-effects whole-brain analyses (reported in main text and supplementary tables/figures), and used SPM8 for processing on a 4T scanner. Participant demographics and cue types are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity fMRI studies with whole-brain task activation maps.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues (ISIS) to assess cue-reactivity in nicotine-dependent smokers and matched nonsmokers. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (Smoking > neutral) and multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM8) with reported cluster thresholds and MNI coordinates. Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although the sample size is small and some analyses are fixed-effects, all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues in abstinent alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. It includes within-participant contrasts of alcohol-associated > control stimuli, reports group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (second-level SPM99) with reported activations (tables/figures), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria and is appropriate for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food) with clear within-subject contrasts (WATCH Food > WATCH Neutral) and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses. The methods report whole-brain statistical mapping (thresholding, random-effects one-/two-sample t-tests) and include reported coordinates for regressions; scanner field strength (3T), processing software (SPM8), participant age and sex, and cue type are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This publication is a study protocol (pre-registered trial) that describes methods for an rtfMRI neurofeedback intervention including a cue-reactivity paradigm using visual alcohol images, participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, it contains no original fMRI results or group-level whole-brain activation maps and reports no within-participant contrasts (drug-cues > control) or statistical maps. Thus it does not provide the task-evoked whole-brain empirical data required for inclusion. It is therefore excluded under E6 (non-empirical/methods-only paper without original human fMRI data).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of opioid cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (opioid words). It includes within-participant contrasts (opioid-word vs. neutral-word, OW>NW) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM second-level analyses (one-sample and two-sample t-tests) used to define activations. Methods report participant demographics, cue type (opioid words), MRI scanner field strength (3T Philips), and processing software (AFNI for despiking, SPM12 for preprocessing and analysis). Although the paper also includes connectivity (DCM) analyses, univariate whole-brain task activation maps are reported and described, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking-related vs control images). The authors report within-participant contrasts (e.g., whole-brain contrasts/ANCOVAs for “smoke > control”), a group-level, whole-brain random-effects ANOVA and RFX ANCOVAs with cluster-level correction, and report results in tables/figures. Participant age and sex are provided, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager) are reported. The paper contains full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all meta-analysis inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity that includes visual smoking cues and directly compares smoking-related versus neutral picture blocks within participants (CIG-I > NEU-I). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster Z>2.3, p<0.05) with detailed results described in text and figures/tables. Necessary study descriptors are provided: participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI investigation of effort-based motivation for monetary reward in alcohol-dependent participants, not a cue-reactivity task using drug-related or natural reward visual stimuli. It does not include within-participant contrasts of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli. Although it provides group-level whole-brain task activation maps and reports participant and methods details, it fails to meet the primary inclusion requirements (I3 and I4) for cue-reactivity using visual drug/natural reward stimuli. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of visual cocaine cue-reactivity with within-participant cue>baseline contrasts and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (tables/coordinates). Participant age/sex, cue type (cocaine), and MRI field strength (1.5T) are reported. However, the paper does not specify the fMRI processing/statistical software (e.g., SPM, AFNI, FSL) required by I7. Because not all inclusion criteria are met (specifically I7), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (drug images tailored to cocaine, alcohol, nicotine). It reports within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral cues at first-level and group-level second-level, random-effects, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with cluster correction and tables/coordinates/figures. Methods state MRI field strength (3.0T Siemens Trio) and preprocessing/analysis software (SPM12; AFNI 3dClustSim used). Participant age/sex and cue types are reported. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

Full text provided is limited to title and abstract (fulltext_incomplete=true). Based on the abstract, this is an fMRI study using script-guided imagery (internal/ auditory cues), not visual cue stimuli, so it does not meet I3 (visual-stimulus cue-reactivity). The reported contrasts compare drug-cue imagery versus stress imagery rather than drug-cue versus a neutral/control visual stimulus, so I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli) is not satisfied. Although voxelwise results are reported in the abstract, the incomplete full text prevents verification of whole-brain, unmasked group-level maps and other required reporting (I5, I6, I7). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses visual alcohol cues within a hybrid task and reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol versus neutral/scrambled images. Second-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM8 with cluster/FWE correction and resulting clusters/coordinates are reported. Relevant metadata are provided (participant ages range, sex noted, cue type = alcohol, 3T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of cigarettes vs neutral pens) presented alongside partner/acquaintance images. The study reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., acquaintance+cigarette vs acquaintance+pen; partner+cigarette vs partner+pen) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction (AFNI). Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual heroin-related and pleasant (natural reward) images in an abstinent opioid-dependent and control sample. It reports within-subject contrasts (heroin vs baseline/neutral; pleasant vs baseline), and group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (results reported with coordinates and FDR-corrected thresholds). Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, cue types, 3T scanner field strength, SPM2 processing). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full-text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of alcohol (drug) and food (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual cues (500 ms cue symbols). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., high-threat alcohol cues vs high-threat food/neutral cues) and task-evoked analyses. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (AFNI 3dMVM, cluster correction via 3dClustSim) with results described in the text and referenced figures/tables. Necessary metadata are provided: participant demographics (age/sex), cue types (alcohol, food, neutral), scanner field strength (Siemens Prisma 3T), and processing software (AFNI). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in active cocaine users, with within-subject contrasts comparing cocaine-related vs neutral backgrounds. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps were computed and thresholded (voxelwise t, cluster correction) and reported in the results (clusters/ROIs), meeting the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Methods report scanner field strength (3T General Electric Signa) and processing software (AFNI), and participant age/sex and cue type (cocaine) are detailed. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for visual drug cue-reactivity fMRI and reports necessary methodological details.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity that used visual cues (abstract shapes predicting beer vs water) and included within-subject contrasts (beer>water) for anticipation/outcome/delivery phases. The authors report group-level, whole-brain one-sample t-tests and ANOVAs for the beer>water contrasts (with thresholding and coordinates), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The manuscript provides participant age/sex (male, ages 18–25), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T Prisma), and processing software (SPM8), and reports results in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This full-text reports an empirical fMRI study using visual drug cues (cannabis) in cannabis-dependent adults. It includes within-subject contrasts of cannabis cues > Gaussian baseline and cannabis cues > nature/food, using group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses conducted in SPM5 on a 3T scanner, with results reported as clusters/regions and correlations. Participant age/sex, cue types, scanner field strength, and processing software are all reported. The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity.

The study is an empirical whole-brain fMRI investigation of neural responses to emotionally arousing IAPS images (positive and negative) versus neutral images. While it meets methodological reporting requirements (whole-brain voxelwise analyses, scanner/processing details, participant age/sex reported), it does not assess drug cue-reactivity or clearly defined natural reward-related cue-reactivity (e.g., food or sexual cues) as required by the meta-analysis objective. The within-subject contrasts are positive>neutral and negative>neutral for general emotional stimuli, not drug cues or specified natural reward cues. Therefore key inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are not met, so the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite satisfying I5, I6, and I7.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual pictorial stimuli, reporting within-subject contrasts (smoking-related > neutral) and group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results (thresholds and cluster extents) and reported peak coordinates. Methods report participant age/sex (male, mean age), cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM5). Results include whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables as well as regression analyses of cue-evoked activity. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and is complete for screening purposes.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation (3T scanner) of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related stimuli in treatment-seeking smokers. It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking-related cues > neutral cues and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (tables and figures) analyzed with FSL. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength, and processing software are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

The study is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual alcohol stimuli, includes within-subject contrast 'alcohol > neutral', reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (voxel-wise thresholds and cluster-extent correction) and provides required sample demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing software (SPM). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of cannabis cue reactivity that includes visual (picture) stimuli and reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., cannabis picture > baseline; cannabis picture > flower picture). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-thresholded maps and described in text/tables/figures). Participant age and sex, cue type (cannabis/pictures), MRI field strength (3.0T), and processing software (FSL, AFNI, ANTS) are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual beverage photographs embedded as distractors. The authors report within-participant contrasts comparing alcohol distractors vs. non-alcohol distractors (AD > NAD/AD-NAD), and perform group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (rmANOVA and voxelwise correlations) with multiple-comparison correction. Methods report MRI field strength (3T) and processing software (AFNI, SPM5), and participant age and sex distributions are described. Whole-brain results are described and thresholded (FWE-corrected clusters), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes unmasked whole-brain task effects, empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study in heroin-dependent participants using heroin-related audiovisual (including visual) cues and matched neutral controls, with within-subject (pre/post) contrasts and heroin vs neutral condition comparisons. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster correction and reported peak coordinates; mean % BOLD changes were extracted and regionwise statistics provided. Participant age/sex, cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus all required inclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a visual alcohol cue-reactivity task (alcohol vs neutral pictures) with within-subject contrasts (alcohol > neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM, cluster correction via AlphaSim) and results are described with cluster-level findings; participant age range, gender, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T Siemens), and processing software (SPM) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual drug-cue fMRI whole-brain task activation reporting.

Although this is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli with within-participant alcohol>neutral contrasts (meets I3 and I4), the report presents only anatomically- and functionally-defined ROI analyses and striatum-masked voxelwise results. The paper does not report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map required by I5. Therefore it falls under exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). The full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using audiovisual (visual) smoking vs nonsmoking stimuli, with within-subject contrasts (smoking cues > nonsmoking cues) before and after medication. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM5) with suprathreshold clusters and coordinates in tables/figures, and provides participant demographics (Table 1) and cue type. Imaging processing software (SPM5) is reported; imaging acquisition details are referenced and available in the eAppendix. The manuscript contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and reports whole-brain task activation maps and coordinate tables suitable for meta-analysis of task-evoked cue reactivity. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This article is a narrative review rather than an empirical fMRI study. The full text summarizes theoretical and animal research and discusses fMRI and phMRI applications, but it contains no original human fMRI methods, participant data, task contrasts (e.g., within-participant cue>control contrasts), whole-brain statistical maps, or reported coordinates. Therefore it does not meet the review’s requirement for original, whole-brain task-evoked fMRI data and meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original human fMRI data). The provided full text appears complete (introduction, discussion, conclusions); however, no primary fMRI results are reported.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol-related cues and neutral controls, reporting within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs neutral) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2). The paper provides participant age and sex (male, ages reported), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM2). Whole-brain results and coordinates are reported; small-volume correction was also used for a priori VOIs but whole-brain voxelwise analyses and between-group tests are present. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is original human fMRI task activation data).
