This is an fMRI study of visual smoking cue-reactivity in nicotine-dependent humans that reports a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast and presents group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation results (cluster reported with MNI coordinates) using FSL Randomise. Participant sex and age information are reported, cue type is nicotine (visual stimuli), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are described. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual cannabis and other emotionally evocative cues with within-subject contrasts (cannabis>neutral, sexual>neutral, aversive>neutral). The methods report participant demographics (age/sex), cue types, 3.0-T scanner field strength, and SPM8 preprocessing/analysis. Although primary ROI-based thresholding was emphasized, the manuscript states that whole-brain analyses were performed and are reported (Online Resource 2) as tables of results, satisfying the requirement that at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map is available and acceptable if presented in tables/supplement. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

Although this is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts and full reporting of participant demographics and scanner/software (meets I3, I4, I7), the primary analyses are ROI-based MVPA in the lateral occipital complex. The paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for cigarette>control (or equivalent) contrasts — only a whole-brain localizer for object regions and ROI-based results are presented. Therefore it lacks the required whole-brain task activation map (I5) and must be excluded per E3 (ROI-only results without whole-brain task maps). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual smoking cues (hand holding a cigarette) and neutral control images, with within-participant contrasts of smoking cue > neutral described. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (cluster-level FWE results and voxelwise ROI-corrected results) in the text and gives coordinates; scanner field strength (3.0T), processing software (SPM12, CONN), participant age/sex (male-only) and cue type (nicotine) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of methamphetamine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in humans. It includes a within-subject Methamphetamine Cue>Control Cue contrast and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps (cluster-corrected Z>2.3/p<0.05) and associated tables/figures. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type (methamphetamine) is specified, MRI field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL) are described. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and provides the required whole-brain task activation evidence, so it meets all inclusion criteria I3–I7.

Although this is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (I3) with within-subject ALC>BEV contrasts (I4) and reports demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software (I7), the paper reports ROI-based analyses (extraction of BOLD timecourses from 6-mm spheres and hierarchical models) and does not present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation map or whole-brain results. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain task map). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images) with within-subject contrasts (COC > NEU). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses for the COC > NEU contrast (between-group t-tests) and describes within-group activations; it provides participant age/sex, cue type (cocaine), MRI field strength (3.0T) and processing software (BrainVoyager). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

The study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. It uses an individualized guided-imagery (auditory/script) task rather than visual stimuli, so it fails I3. Additionally, the paper reports voxel-wise connectivity (ICD) and seed-based connectivity analyses during task periods but does not report task-evoked whole-brain activation contrasts (e.g., food>control) required by the review; thus it falls under exclusion criterion E4 (connectivity-only without a whole-brain task activation map). No qualifying within-participant visual cue>control whole-brain activation maps are provided. Full text appears complete.

This is a within-subjects fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine-related) and control images; it reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (mixed-model ANOVA) with results surviving FDR correction in ventral striatum and additional whole-brain activations reported (tables/figures). Participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM2) are provided. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI visual cue-reactivity studies and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (tobacco) with within-participant contrasts (tobacco vs neutral and tobacco vs money). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (disjunction mask, cluster thresholds, AlphaSim correction) and presents cluster results and coordinates. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (AFNI) are all reported. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, reporting within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral cues and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (with tables/figures and corrected thresholds). Relevant participant details (age/sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study reports resting-state functional connectivity and correlational analyses of salience network coupling and ADHD symptoms in smokers versus non-smokers. It does not include any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm using visual drug or natural reward cues, nor any within-participant contrast of drug-cue > control stimuli. No group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or activation contrasts are reported. Therefore it fails the meta-analysis inclusion criteria requiring task-based visual cue-reactivity fMRI and instead meets exclusion criteria for resting-state/seed-based connectivity-only studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol, non-alcoholic beverage, control pictures). The paper includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol > beverage) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses conducted in SPM99 with cluster-level results and Talairach coordinates reported (tables and figures). Key methodological details are provided: participant demographics (male and female college students), cue type (alcohol visual pictures), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM99). Whole-brain results are reported as coordinates and statistical maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study using visual alcohol cues with within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise results. However, the full text does not report the MRI scanner field strength, which is required by inclusion criterion I7 (it requires reporting participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software). Because I7 is not satisfied, the study cannot be included in the meta-analysis despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual alcohol-picture stimuli. The manuscript reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs. neutral) as the primary outcome, and a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise linear mixed-effects model in AFNI with cluster-corrected results presented in tables/figures. Key metadata required by the review are present (participant ages and sex, cue type: alcohol, scanner field strength: 3.0T, processing software: AFNI). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual drug-related cue reactivity.

This paper reports an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual photographic cues in dependent smokers, with within-subject contrasts (smoking > control) computed and tested at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5). The manuscript includes full methods (participants, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing), results (tables/figures of whole-brain activations and coordinates), and participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, scanner field strength (4.0 T), and processing software. The full text is provided (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (with an added taste sip). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol beverage cues > nonalcohol beverage cues) and presents group-level voxelwise statistical maps from spatially normalized SPM analyses (cluster-thresholded whole-brain analyses within the imaged volume). Participant age and sex are reported, cue type is alcohol, scanner field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (MEDx/SPM99) are specified. Results are reported in tables/figures and described in the text. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study is an fMRI investigation of cocaine cue reactivity using audiovisual (including visual) stimuli and reports within-subject cocaine>neutral contrasts. However, the analyses are focused on single-slice, region-of-interest (vermian ROIs) measures (percent change and spatial extent) rather than reporting a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or whole-brain coordinate tables. The manuscript does not present unmasked whole-brain statistical maps or clear whole-brain voxelwise group results, and processing software is not specified. Therefore it violates the review's exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting with no whole-brain results) and fails to meet I5 (whole-brain voxelwise map) and I7 (processing software reporting).

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking vs neutral images). The authors report a within-participant contrast (smoking > neutral) and assess correlations with behavioral attentional bias. Analyses are group-level whole-brain (random-effects ANCOVA) with cluster-level multiple-comparisons correction; whole-brain results are reported with coordinates, cluster volumes, and figures/tables. Participant age and sex are provided (women, mean age), scanner field strength (Siemens Trio 3T) and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Thus all required inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is an fMRI cannabis cue-reactivity study using visual cues, but the paper reports only dynamic functional connectivity and topological/network analyses (DCC-derived connectivity measures) rather than any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps or coordinates for a drug-cue > control contrast. Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or equivalent coordinate reporting) is not met; the study therefore falls under exclusion criterion E4 (connectivity-only analyses without whole-brain task activation). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (personal and standard smoking vs nonsmoking images). It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking>nonsmoking stimuli (e.g., PSE>PNE, smoking>nonsmoking), and reports group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (cluster-corrected whole-brain results and supplementary table/figures). Participant demographic details (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are all reported. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study using visual cue videos (smoking and food) with within-subject contrasts (Smoking>Food, Smoking>Baseline, Food>Baseline). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FLAME; coordinate tables and figures provided), processing software (FMRIB/FSL) and scanner field strength (Siemens 3T) are described, and participant age/sex and cue types are reported. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a resting-state functional connectivity/graph-theory study of intrinsic brain networks in smokers, not a task-based cue-reactivity fMRI study using visual stimuli. The paper does not report any within-participant drug-cue > control-stimulus contrasts or task-evoked whole-brain statistical maps; analyses are resting-state connectivity (partial correlations, graph metrics). Therefore it fails the review inclusion requirements and meets exclusion criterion E4 (resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine) with within-subject contrasts (smoking cues > neutral cues). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses were performed using SPM5 and results are reported with coordinates/tables (and figures) for pre- and post-smoking contrasts. Relevant details are provided (participant age and sex, cue type, 3.0 T scanner field strength, and processing software). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes an unmasked whole-brain task activation map). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The paper is a task-based fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol > neutral) at the group level. Whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses are described (flexible factorial, two-sample and paired t tests) with cluster thresholds and small-volume FWE corrections; peak coordinates and cluster results are reported. Participant age/sex information, cue type (alcohol visual cues), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are all provided. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). It does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity, or between-group-only contrasts. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study that includes visual smoking cues (video) and within-participant contrasts (smoking>baseline; alcohol>baseline). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (voxel-wise t-tests, cluster-wise inference), with results described in figures and cluster statistics. Participant age/sex, cue types, 3T scanner field strength, and processing software (FSL) are reported. Although the alcohol task used taste cues, the study contains visual cue-reactivity data meeting the review objective for visual stimuli, and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is a BOLD fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity with a within-subject Alcohol>Water contrast and whole-brain voxelwise results (and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software), the cue modality is gustatory (alcohol taste delivered via gustometer) rather than visual stimuli. The meta-analysis objective and inclusion criterion I3 require cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Therefore the study does not meet the required inclusion criterion (I3) and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) visual cue-reactivity with an within-subject smoking>neutral contrast and reports whole-brain voxelwise group results (tables/Supplement). It therefore meets I3, I4, I5, and I6. However the full text provided does not report MRI scanner field strength (e.g., 1.5T/3T) and does not give explicit participant age range (only "college students") in the main text; inclusion criterion I7 requires reporting of participant age and sex, cue type, MRI scanner field strength, and processing software. Processing software (FSL), cue type (nicotine), and sex (male) are reported, but MRI field strength and clear age information are not. Because not all required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I7 missing), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of food (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images). The design includes within-subject contrasts of food vs. matched object control stimuli, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects FLAME in FSL) with permutation-based cluster correction. The paper reports participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3 T Siemens Skyra), and processing software (FSL), satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smokers viewing cigarette-related and other emotional (including erotic) visual stimuli. It reports within-subject whole-brain group-level analyses (cigarette > neutral) using a random-effects GLM, provides cluster coordinates/tables, and compares drug cues to naturally rewarding stimuli. Participant age range and sex distribution, cue type (nicotine/cigarette), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are all reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes a within-participant contrast (alcohol vs. control pictures), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation (1-sample t-test; Table 2 and Figure 2) and ROI analyses, and provides participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM5). Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the supplied full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are violated. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of alcohol (visual drinking cues) with within-subject contrasts (drinking cues > neutral) and reports participant age/sex, scanner (3T) and SPM preprocessing (satisfying I3, I4, I7), the analyses are ROI-based (ventral striatum and MPFC) and the paper does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or coordinates for whole-brain results. This violates the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and therefore falls under exclusion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain maps). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI task-development pilot using orally delivered alcohol tastes with visual written cues that signal upcoming taste; primary contrasts and reported cue-reactivity analyses focus on taste delivery (alcohol taste > water taste) and prediction-error effects rather than visual cue-induced cue-reactivity. The meta-analysis requires studies assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3) and at least one within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli using visual cues (I4). These visual-stimulus cue-reactivity criteria are not met. The full text is complete and the paper does report whole-brain results and methodological details (scanner, software, demographics), but it does not provide a within-subject contrast of visual drug cues > control visual stimuli. Therefore it must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol-associated cues in abstinent alcohol-dependent participants and controls. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol-associated > control stimuli, and group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM99 (results thresholded and reported in tables/figures). Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, cue type: alcohol, scanner field strength: 1.5T, processing software: SPM99). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task map, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol images in college-aged participants (ages 18–21). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs. non-alcohol beverage images) and repetition contrasts (second vs. first presentation). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed with cluster-based whole-brain correction and results reported in tables/figures/text. Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, cue type: alcohol, 3T Siemens scanner, processing in SPM5). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes whole-brain task effects). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual reward/drug cue-reactivity.

The study is an fMRI investigation with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses, within-subject contrasts of drug-cue versus neutral stimuli, and reports participant age/sex, cue type (cocaine/alcohol), scanner (3T Siemens Trio), and software (AFNI). However, inclusion criterion I3 requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli; this study used individualized script-driven (auditory/imagery) cues rather than visual cue presentations. Because it fails to meet I3 (visual-stimulus modality), it does not satisfy all inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

The study does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the cue modality is gustatory (alcohol taste delivered via tubing) rather than visual stimuli. Although brief visual labels (“Alcohol Taste”/“Control Taste”) were presented, the primary cue exposure and task stimulus were taste-based, and the meta-analysis requires visual cue-reactivity paradigms. The study does meet other inclusion criteria (within-subject alcohol>water contrast, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates, and reporting of participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software), but failure to satisfy I3 requires exclusion.

Although this is an fMRI study of nicotine cue reactivity (participants exposed to cigarette vs neutral cues) and includes within-subject comparisons, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps. Analyses focus on ROI-based activation and directed/effective connectivity (uSEM/GIMME) without accompanying unmasked whole-brain task activation results. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria for studies reporting only ROI/effective connectivity analyses without whole-brain results. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol-cue > neutral (and stress > neutral) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (p<.001, cluster-corrected) with figures and supplemental tables. Relevant participant demographics (age range, sex), cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BioImageSuite; AFNI used for cluster correction) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a resting-state seed-based functional connectivity study comparing smokers and nonsmokers and assessing acute smoking effects. It does not present any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm using visual drug or natural-reward cues, provides no within-participant contrast of drug-cue > control stimuli, and reports no whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity fMRI studies and meets exclusion criterion E4 (seed-based/connectivity or resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue‑reactivity paradigms (video films) with heroin cues and neutral control stimuli. It includes within‑participant contrasts (heroin‑cue vs neutral) and a group‑level, whole‑brain voxelwise 2×2 factorial analysis reported with Talairach coordinates, tables, and figures. Key methodological details required by the review are reported: participant age/sex, cue type (heroin), MRI field strength (1.5T), and processing software (AFNI). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI‑only, not connectivity‑only, not non‑empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli in alcohol-dependent patients and controls. It includes within-subject contrasts (alcohol cues > neutral cues) at the single-subject level and group-level analyses. Although primary reported findings are ROI-corrected, the manuscript explicitly reports whole-brain (uncorrected) exploratory activations in the Supplementary material (i.e., group-level, voxelwise task-evoked maps), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain results reported in text/tables/supplement. Relevant details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3 T scanner, SPM12 processing) are provided. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are violated.

This is an fMRI study of visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts (e.g., fattening food > object), and reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner (3T) and software (FSL). However, group analyses were conducted using a region-of-interest (ROI) approach only, and the authors explicitly state they “limited our investigation to regions of interest.” No unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level activation map is reported. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of visual smoking cue reactivity and includes within-participant smoking>neutral contrasts and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL/FreeSurfer). However, the manuscript reports analyses based on extracting beta weights from predefined ROIs (left/right NAc and caudate) rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map, nor are whole-brain results (coordinates/figures/tables) reported. Therefore it violates the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related pictures. It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > neutral (crave and resist conditions), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using FSL/FEAT with FLAME (Z>2.3, cluster p=0.05). Whole-brain results are presented in tables of coordinates and figures. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3–I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The provided full-text appears to be only the abstract (methods/results summary) and is incomplete (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract we can confirm this is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward), so I3 is satisfied. However, the abstract does not provide sufficient detail to confirm required inclusion criteria: no clear within-participant contrast of cue>control stimuli is reported (I4 not verifiable), no statement that group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps were reported (I5 not verifiable), and scanner field strength and processing software are not reported (I7 not satisfied). Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be verified, the study cannot be included.

This study does not investigate drug- or natural reward–related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It is a within-subject fMRI study of resting-state network coupling and a working memory (N-back) task comparing 24-hour nicotine abstinence vs smoking satiety. No drug-cue exposure paradigm or within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli is reported, and there are no whole-brain task-evoked maps of cue-reactivity. Thus it fails key inclusion criteria (notably I3 and I4/I5) for the review. Full text is complete and was reviewed.

This is an fMRI study using visual alcohol-related cues (alcohol pictures) with within-participant contrasts of alcohol-related > neutral pictures. The methods describe voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (voxelwise t-tests, whole-brain corrected thresholds, Talairach coordinates and reported cluster/coordinate results), and seed-based/resting analyses in addition. Relevant metadata are provided: participant numbers and ages, cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (TurboBrainVoyager/BrainVoyager, AFNI, FSL). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain cue-reactivity using visual stimuli are met (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7). No exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an fMRI study of a natural reward (juice) with a visual cue and reports sufficient participant and scanning details, the paper's results are reported primarily as a priori ROI analyses. The manuscript does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or an explicit within-participant contrast of reward-predictive visual cues versus neutral/control visual stimuli. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results and a within-participant cue>control analysis required for inclusion. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). It includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol > soft drink) at the single-subject level and reports group-level second-level t tests on these contrasts. Although primary inferential tests used small-volume correction in a priori ROIs, the authors explicitly report exploratory whole-brain analyses (in the online supplement and Table S1), satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (reported in text/tables/supplement). Relevant methodological details are provided (3T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing) and participant demographics/sex are reported (male participants; sample size and reference to Table 1). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical 3T BOLD fMRI study in cocaine-dependent humans using visual cue stimuli (cocaine, sexual, aversive, neutral) with a backward-masking paradigm. First-level within-subject contrasts (cocaine vs neutral, sex vs neutral, aversive vs neutral) were created and group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level analyses were performed and reported (cluster-corrected results and peak coordinates in Table 2). The paper reports whole-brain task-evoked maps (both group comparisons and single-group placebo task effects) and provides participant age/sex, cue types, scanner field strength, and processing software (SPM8). Results are reported with coordinates and cluster correction. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual reward-related cue-reactivity fMRI and does not violate exclusion criteria.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual smoking and food cues (relevant to the review), the analyses do not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for drug>control or reward>control contrasts. The paper uses ICA-derived network spatial maps and component betas (temporal sorting of Smoke and Food) and reports network-level (DMN/ECN/SN) betas and contrasts (Smoke vs Food). This is a connectivity/component-based approach without an unmasked voxelwise task activation map or a drug>neutral contrast, so it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore it must be excluded under E4.

This fMRI study uses visual smoking cues and reports within-subject contrasts (smoking > neutral), and reports whole-brain task-evoked analyses with coordinate tables. However it does not report all required participant and scanner details per inclusion criterion I7: participant sex is not specified and MRI scanner field strength is not reported in the provided full text. Because I7 is not satisfied, the study does not meet all inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol cues > non-alcohol beverage cues) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects statistical maps (SPM5; threshold p<.005, cluster extent 15 voxels) with tables/figures describing activated regions. Scanner field strength (3.0 T), processing software (SPM5), and cue type (alcohol) are reported; demographic information (Table 1) and mention of age/sex are included in the full text. The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

The provided full-text content is incomplete—only metadata/header information and citation details are present (no Introduction, Methods, Results, or Discussion). Because core article content is missing, I cannot verify whether the study meets inclusion criteria I3–I7 (e.g., that it is an fMRI study using visual drug-related cues, includes within-participant drug-cue>control contrasts, reports whole-brain voxelwise maps or coordinate tables, and provides participant demographics and scanner/processing details). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) can be confidently applied based on the truncated content. To determine eligibility this study’s complete article (methods and results) or supplementary materials must be provided.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual/video stimuli, includes within-participant contrasts (craving-inducing cues vs mosaic control; aversion-inducing cues vs mosaic), and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results (voxelwise SPMs with FDR thresholds and reported cluster-wise findings). Methods report scanner field strength (1.5T) and processing software (BrainVoyager BVQX 1.9); participant demographics (age and sex) are described in the text as compared between groups and group sizes are given. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Meets all required inclusion criteria and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is a human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes visual stimuli (food pictures). Subject-level contrasts included HFHS vs LFLS, HFHS vs NF, and HFHS vs rest for pictures; group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM12, 3T scanner) reporting cluster results and extracted beta values. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength, and processing software are reported. Although many group tests focus on pre-to-post (surgery) changes, the study computed the requisite within-participant cue>control contrasts and produced whole-brain group-level maps of these contrasts (as pre-post difference maps). Thus the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for fMRI visual natural reward cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI study in AUD participants but it does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug/food/sexual cues. The tasks used emotional faces (angry/fearful vs. forms) and a dot-probe for attentional bias to emotional expressions, not alcohol-related visual cues. Therefore it does not provide a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast required for inclusion. The study does report whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps and provides coordinates and processing details (SPM, AFNI, 3T scanner, age/sex), but it fails key inclusion criteria I3 and I4. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual cue videos. Within-participant contrasts (crave-allow vs neutral; crave-resist vs neutral; crave-allow vs crave-resist) are reported. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using FSL/FLAME with cluster-corrected z-thresholds and results are reported in tables and figures (local maxima coordinates and images). Methods report MRI field strength (1.5 T), processing software (FSL FEAT), cue type (nicotine/cigarette videos), and demographic comparisons (sex, demographics in Table 1), satisfying required participant information. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, contains within-participant task effects and whole-brain maps, empirical data). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study used fMRI and visual word stimuli and performed whole-brain voxelwise analyses, but its primary reported contrasts concern monetary reward (50¢>0¢). Although drug-related and neutral words were presented, the authors report no within-subject analyses or whole-brain results contrasting drug cues > control (drug>neutral) and explicitly collapsed across word type. Therefore it does not provide the required within-participant cue-reactivity contrast (I4) needed for inclusion in this meta-analysis of drug/natural reward cue-reactivity. It does report whole-brain maps and participant/scan/process details, but the absence of any drug-cue>control whole-brain task effect prevents inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of cocaine cue reactivity using visual stimuli (cocaine vs neutral pictures). The paper reports a within-participant contrast (cocaine cues > neutral cues) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-thresholded statistic images, cluster sizes, and coordinates reported in Table 2 and figures). Scanner field strength (3T), processing software (FSL), participant sex counts and ages/matching information, and cue type (cocaine visual cues) are all provided. Although the paper also reports effective connectivity analyses, it additionally reports unmasked whole-brain task activation maps, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

The study does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it used gustatory (taste) cues delivered via a gustometer (alcohol taste vs. juice), not visual stimuli. Although it satisfies other criteria — within-participant Alcohol>Juice contrast (I4), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and coordinates/figures (I5, I6), and reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software (I7) — failure to use visual cue modalities required by the review means it must be excluded. Full text appears complete for evaluation.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with fasting participants, satisfying the review’s focus on visual cue-reactivity. Within-subject contrasts of food>neutral (scrambled) images were computed and entered into group-level analyses. The paper reports a group-level whole-brain one-sample t-test (FDR-corrected) showing task-evoked activation across limbic and visual regions, meeting the requirement for a voxelwise whole-brain task map; although the primary between-group comparison was ROI-restricted, whole-brain task results are reported and described in the text. Key methodological details are provided (3T scanner, SPM5, cue type = food, sample size and matching for age/sex). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is not an fMRI investigation: it uses transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), EMG and motor-evoked potentials to assess corticobulbar excitability in smokers during visual cue exposure. It does not report any functional MRI data, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps, or voxelwise activation results. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (functional MRI study) and does not provide the required fMRI whole-brain contrasts (I4–I6). The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not meet the meta-analysis’ stimulus modality requirement. Although it is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity with within-subject alcohol-cue > neutral contrasts and whole-brain task maps (and reports participant demographics, scanner strength, and processing software), the alcohol cues were individualized, auditorily-presented guided-imagery scripts (auditory/imagined cues), not visual stimuli. The meta-analysis requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3). All other relevant inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues with a within-subject contrast (‘favourite drinks > neutral’) and group-level second-level analyses. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (P<0.001 uncorrected) with coordinates and ROI SVC results; participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug/food/sexual cues. It uses a probabilistic delay-discounting task with monetary rewards, not presentation of alcohol or other substance cues, and contains no within-subject contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli. Although the paper reports group-level whole-brain fMRI task activation maps (satisfying I5/I6) and provides participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software, it fails to meet critical inclusion criteria I3 (cue-reactivity using visual drug/natural reward cues) and I4 (within-participant drug-cue > control contrast); cue type is monetary rather than a target cue type (alcohol images, food, sexual, etc.). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the article is not eligible for this meta-analysis.

This paper is an empirical human fMRI study using visual tobacco advertisement stimuli to probe cue reactivity in smokers and never-smokers. It reports within-subject contrasts (tobacco > control advertisement) at the individual level and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with cluster-level FDR correction; results are presented as statistical maps and described in text/tables. Participant age and sex (male only), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly assesses cue-reactivity to visual drug (cocaine) and natural reward (food) stimuli using video paradigms. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (cocaine>neutral and food>neutral), whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with cluster-level FWE correction, and provides tables/figures of results. Participant demographics (age, male sex), cue types, scanner field strength (4T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study of marijuana cue reactivity using visual stimuli in treatment-seeking, marijuana-dependent participants. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of MJ cues > non-MJ cues, conducted group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) and reports significant activations with tables/figures; an unmasked whole-brain display is also referenced. Relevant participant demographics (age, sex distribution), cue type (cannabis), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM2) are provided. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine-related cue-reactivity using visual smoking vs neutral images (within-subject smoke>neutral contrast). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results (task main effect smoke>neutral) with cluster-thresholded maps (Z>2.3, p=0.05) and PPI connectivity analyses; task activation results are reported in tables/figures. Methods report participant demographics (Table 1), cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues (I3) with a within-subject contrast heroin-related > neutral (I4). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using FSL/FLAME with cluster correction and results reported (I5/I6). The paper reports participant ages/sex (male), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (FSL/FEAT) (I7). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual drug cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videos). It includes within-participant contrasts (smoking > non-smoking control videos), reports group-level voxelwise statistical maps and t-maps with correction and peak coordinates (tables/figures), and provides required participant and methods details (age, sex, cue type nicotine, 3 T scanner, processing software NIAK/fmristat). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary tables/figures are referenced. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol cue- and stress-related neural responses, with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and appropriate reporting of age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner (3T), and processing software. However, the cue paradigm used individualized audiotaped imagery scripts (auditory/imagery cues), not visual stimuli. The meta-analysis requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3), which is not met. Other inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied, but failure to meet I3 leads to exclusion. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes a within-subject contrast (smoking cues > neutral stimuli), performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM99) with reported thresholding and clusters, and reports coordinates/tables/figures. Participant age and sex (10 male smokers, mean age 32), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM99) are all provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant task activation maps, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This study is an fMRI investigation of opioid cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in detoxified OUD patients. It reports within-subject contrasts of drug versus neutral stimuli, includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain ANOVA with reported cluster in ventral striatum/mOFC), and provides participant age/sex, cue types, scanner field strength (Siemens Tim Trio 3T) and processing software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts and adequate reporting of age/sex, cue type, scanner (3T), and processing software (AFNI). However, the report uses an a priori ROI approach for group-level inference (averaging parameter estimates within 5-mm spheres) and presents ROI statistics rather than an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group activation map. No group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (voxelwise results) are reported. Because the study reports only ROI-based group analyses without whole-brain results, it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain evidence and must be excluded (E3).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using a visual conditioned stimulus (visual cue paired with juice). The paper reports within-subject contrasts for event types including the visual cue (CS) versus baseline/other events, uses whole-brain (WB) voxelwise analyses (reported in text and supplementary tables) and small-volume-corrected analyses, and provides participant demographics (age/sex), cue type (juice as a natural reward), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI). Thus it meets criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity with visual stimuli, within-participant cue contrasts, whole-brain results (reported in text/tables), and necessary methodological details. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this paper is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual drug/alcohol cues and reports within-subject drug/alcohol > neutral contrasts (satisfying I3 and I4) and reports participant demographics and acquisition/processing details (I7), its primary reported analyses are seed-based task-modulated functional connectivity (gPPI) across predefined ROIs. The manuscript does not present or describe a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map for the drug>control contrast. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (seed-based/effective connectivity only without whole-brain task maps). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures indicating puffs vs money vs neutral). It reports within-subject contrasts (puff>neutral and money>neutral) comparing abstinent and nonabstinent states. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and reported (exploratory whole-brain maps at p<.001 with cluster threshold), and key methodological/reporting details are provided (participant ages and sex, cue type: nicotine, scanner field strength 3.0T, processing software SPM8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete for screening. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This full text reports an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures) with an in-scanner sip prime. It includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol cues > beverage cues) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM96) with thresholded statistical maps and tables/figures of activated regions. Scanner field strength (1.5T), processing software (SPM96), participant age/sex, and cue type (alcohol visual cues) are all described. The manuscript contains complete core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical study).

This study is an event-related fMRI investigation using visual heroin-related cues in methadone-maintained patients. It reports within-participant contrasts of heroin-related stimuli > neutral stimuli at the group level (one-sample and paired t tests across subjects) and presents voxelwise activation maps (figure and text) derived from whole-brain mixed-effects analyses (with a priori ROI masks used for reporting). Key required details are present: participant age/sex, cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software (FSL). The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (drug words) presented during scanning. It reports within-subject contrasts (drug > neutral words), performs voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster-level correction and reports coordinates/tables, and provides participant demographics, cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength (4T), and processing software (SPM2). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; missing supplemental files are acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes unmasked task effects). Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual drug cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

Full text is incomplete/unavailable (page failed to load). The available content only includes title, authors, journal, date, DOI and an error message; core methods/results/discussion are not present. Therefore I cannot verify inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI with visual drug/natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant drug-cue > control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), or I7 (reporting of age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software). Without the full text it is impossible to confirm whole-brain analyses versus ROI/connectivity-only reporting. Per screening instructions, fulltext_incomplete=true and the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual/held stimuli. The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing cigarette versus neutral cues (cue main effect) at the group level using voxel-wise whole-brain analyses, with coordinates and tables. Methods report participant age/sex (male, mean age), cue type (cigarette), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (AFNI/NIS), satisfying reporting requirements. Full paper includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using alcohol-related visual stimuli (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage pictures) and reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol-related trials to control trials (e.g., Alcohol_nogo > Non-alcohol_go and interaction contrasts isolating alcohol effects). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-level FWE-corrected results, tables of coordinates and figures). Relevant participant information (sex proportions, age differences, abstinence duration), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T Siemens) and processing software (SPM8, DARTEL) are provided. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is original empirical data).

This is an empirical human fMRI study of cocaine cue reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of cocaine and paraphernalia). It reports within-participant cocaine>neutral contrasts and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-test and 2×2 mixed-effects ANOVA) with cluster- and voxelwise thresholds, and reports peak coordinates/clusters. Relevant participant information is provided (age range 18–65, men and women, n=25 with final n reported), cue type (cocaine), MRI field strength (Siemens 3.0T), and processing software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cannabis cues and neutral control stimuli, reporting within-subject contrasts (cannabis cue > neutral) and whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and voxelwise t tests). Participant characteristics (male-only sample, group sizes, dependence status) and cue type (cannabis) are reported; fMRI acquisition and processing details are indicated in the methods/supplement. Results include whole-brain task-evoked activation maps described in the text and region coordinates, as well as behavioral–neural contrasts. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes unmasked whole-brain task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images) in nicotine-dependent participants. The study reports within-subject contrasts (smoking > neutral) at the group level, using whole-brain voxelwise analysis with cluster correction, and presents results in tables and figures. Participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

Although this is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli with a within-subject alcohol>control contrast (ALC vs BEV) and reports relevant participant/scanner/processing details, the paper’s imaging analyses are ROI-based (ventral striatum percent signal change) with no reported group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (images of alcoholic drinks vs water) to examine cue-reactivity and Pavlovian-instrumental transfer in alcohol-dependent patients and controls. The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol versus water (alcohol>water) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain results with reported coordinates and a significant right ventral striatum cluster, pFWE-SVC reported). Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking cues with within-subject SC > non-SC contrasts and adequate reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, all voxelwise analyses were conducted within an a priori ROI mask (ROI-restricted voxelwise results) rather than providing an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map. The manuscript therefore reports only ROI-restricted results and does not provide whole-brain task activation maps or unmasked whole-brain coordinate tables, which fails the review’s requirement for whole-brain evidence. Per exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain findings), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using visual smoking cues (audiovisual smoking vs nonsmoking clips) with within-subject contrasts (smoking cues > nonsmoking cues). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (contrast maps entered into group-level analysis; results reported with peak coordinates and figures), and SPM8 and a 3T scanner are reported. Participant sex and demographic information are provided. The paper contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are met and no exclusion criteria are applicable.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual stimuli of natural rewards (food) and reports within-subject contrasts of food cues versus control stimuli (Look Craved > Look Not Craved; Look Craved > Look Neutral). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (whole-brain cluster correction, tables/figures), and requisite participant and methods details are provided (age/sex distribution, cue type = food, 3.0T MRI, SPM8 preprocessing). The study does not fall under exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task activation maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of heroin (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, reporting within-subject heroin-related > neutral contrasts and prospective relapse prediction. The authors performed voxel-wise, group-level random-effects two-sample t-tests (whole-brain analyses) with results reported in tables/figures and cluster coordinates (Monte Carlo correction), and provided participant demographics (male subjects, age referenced), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM8). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual (and auditory) stimuli, reporting within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM. Methods report scanner field strength (1.5T), processing software (SPM5), participant age/sex, and cue type (food). Statistical thresholds and cluster-correction procedures are described and whole-brain activation results are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Thus the study meets all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual-cue fMRI studies of natural reward cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI study of performance feedback in abstinent smokers using a motion-prediction task with emoji feedback, not a cue-reactivity paradigm. It does not present drug-related or natural-reward visual cues (e.g., images of nicotine, alcohol, food, sexual stimuli) nor report any within-participant contrast of drug-cue > control or natural-reward-cue > control. Although the paper includes group-level whole-brain task activation maps and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software, it fails to meet core inclusion criteria I3 and I4 required for a cue-reactivity meta-analysis. Therefore it must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (cocaine-word Stroop) with a within-subject contrast (Cocaine Words > Neutral Words). The authors performed a voxelwise, group-level SPM12 random-effects whole-brain analysis for the CW minus NW contrast (results reported, including uncorrected cluster-level findings and coordinates used for DCM node selection). Participant demographics (age range, majority male), cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength (Philips 3.0T), and preprocessing/software (AFNI for despiking, SPM12) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not an ROI-only, not connectivity-only without whole-brain activation, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of withdrawal-induced craving and structural DTI correlates; it does not present any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm using visual drug or natural-reward cues. There is no within-participant contrast of drug-cue > control stimuli or any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps; analyses are ICA and ACC-seeded resting-state functional connectivity (seed-based rsFC). Therefore it violates the meta-analysis inclusion requirements and meets exclusion criterion E4 (resting-state/seed-based connectivity only, with no whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of cannabis cue-reactivity using visual (word) stimuli with within-subject cannabis>neutral contrasts and reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner (3T) and processing software (SPM8). However, all imaging analyses were performed as a priori ROI-based analyses with small-volume corrections and the manuscript does not report an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of heroin cue-reactivity using visual stimuli that reports within-subject heroin-related > neutral cue contrasts and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with correction; it provides relevant participant information (male subjects), scanner field strength (3T), cue type (heroin), and processing software. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3–I7) and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical study).

Full text is incomplete (page failed to load); only title/metadata are available. Although the title indicates an fMRI study using smoking-related images (suggesting visual cue-reactivity), the full article (methods/results) is not accessible to verify critical inclusion criteria: whether a within-participant drug-cue>control contrast was reported, whether group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (or coordinate tables clearly describing whole-brain results) are provided, and whether participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software are reported. Because I cannot confirm I4, I5, and I7 from the incomplete content, the study cannot be confidently included in the meta-analysis. Recommend retrieving the complete full text and rescreening.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues with a within-subject Heroin>Neutral contrast and group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses. Whole-brain task activations are reported (voxelwise, FDR-corrected) with coordinates in MNI space. Participant demographics (male, age range), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity meta-analysis and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in obese adults. It reports a within-participant contrast of highly desirable > less desirable food images (paired t-test in a cross-over design). Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (SPM8; 3T scanner) with coordinates, cluster size and FWE-corrected p-values provided. Participant age and sex are reported and cue type is food. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual-reward cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of insula functional connectivity following 12 h smoking abstinence. It does not use a task-based visual cue paradigm nor report any within-participant contrasts of drug cues > control stimuli. All reported analyses are seed-based resting-state connectivity (RSFC) and voxelwise resting-state contrasts (abstinence vs satiety), not task-evoked cue-reactivity maps. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I3 or I4 and falls squarely under exclusion criterion E4 (resting-state/seed-based connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map). The full text provided appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol and non-alcohol beverage cues in participants with AUD and healthy controls. It reports within-subject contrasts of each stimulus versus a mosaic baseline (stimulus>control), first-level contrasts taken to second-level random-effects analyses, and whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected statistics. Key study details required by the review are reported (participant age/sex, cue type = alcohol, scanner field strength = 1.5T, processing software = SPM12). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This fMRI study clearly meets several inclusion criteria for the review (visual alcohol-cue task, within-subject alcohol>neutral contrast, and reporting of whole-brain group-level task activation maps using SPM5 on a 3T scanner). However it does not report participants’ sex/gender breakdown (only mean age is given), and the meta-analysis criteria require relevant information regarding participant age and sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software (I7). Because sex information is missing, not all inclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol beverage pictures and emotional faces). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol pictures > control (alcpic > con) and analogous emotion contrasts. Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise using SPM8 with cluster-level correction and results reported in tables and figures (Tables 2–4, figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Participant characteristics (age-/sex-matched groups, N=26 per group), cue type (alcohol images), scanner field strength (GE 3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity meta-analysis and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task activation maps).

This is an fMRI study of stress-induced cocaine craving using personalized guided-imagery (audio) scripts rather than visual drug or natural reward cues. It therefore does not meet I3 (requires visual stimuli) and does not provide a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli as required by I4 (the primary contrasts are stress vs neutral and correlations with craving). The full text appears complete and does report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and coordinate tables, and reports participant demographics, cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength, and analysis software. Those inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7) are met, but failure to meet I3 and I4 necessitates exclusion from this meta-analysis focused on visual cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol-related stimuli (CUEalc) with a within-subject contrast CUEalc > IAPSneutral. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were conducted (SPM8 and BPM), and at least one result is reported as whole-brain FWE-corrected. The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM8), and provides full methods, results, and discussion. The full text appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses visual cigarette cue videos and a within-subject Cigarette Cues vs Neutral Cues contrast. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected Z maps) and provides whole-brain results in tables and figures. Methods report participant age range/sex information, cue type (nicotine/cigarette), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (FSL 4.1). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation of cue reactivity using visual stimuli (videos of cocaine and food). It reports within-participant contrasts of cocaine > food cues and provides voxel-wise, whole-brain task activation results (cluster maps and coordinates) analyzed with AFNI on a Siemens 3T scanner. Participant age and sex are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of visual drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity.

Only the abstract and metadata are available here (no full article text). The abstract indicates an fMRI study using visual heroin cues and reports within-subject activations, so I3 and I4 appear to be met. However, I cannot verify critical requirements: I5 (presence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map) and full reporting required by I7 (participant age is not reported in the abstract). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm whole-brain unmasked task maps or coordinate reporting necessary for inclusion. Therefore the study is excluded pending access to the complete full text.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using audiovisual smoking cues (visual stimuli) with within-participant contrasts (smoking cues > nonsmoking cues). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistics conducted in SPM2 and reported with statistical maps, tables of coordinates, and figures. Participant age and demographic information, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM2) are reported in the methods. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of study methods and outcomes relevant to the review objective.

This study is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity investigation using visual stimuli and within-subject ALC>BEV contrasts, and it reports participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). However, the reported analyses focus on an a priori right ventral striatum ROI (percent signal change extracted with featquery) and bar-lab behavioral outcomes. The full text does not present or describe a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map, coordinate tables, or whole-brain figures/results that would satisfy the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a single-case (n=1) fMRI study reporting pre/post/relapse task activations to alcohol vs non-alcohol images, but it does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical map required by the meta-analysis. The paper reports region activations qualitatively for the single subject and refers to figures/supplement but lacks a group analysis. Additionally, key methodological details required by I7 (MRI scanner field strength and processing software) are not reported in the provided full text. While the study meets I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual alcohol cues) and I4 (within-participant alcohol cues > control contrast), it fails I5 (group-level whole-brain results) and does not fully satisfy I7. Therefore it must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cannabis cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-participant contrast (cannabis images > neutral/control images). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain cluster corrections described) and provides results in the text/tables/figures. Participant age and sex information, cue type (cannabis), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.
