No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of cannabis but it uses a tactile cue-exposure paradigm (tactile presentations of a marijuana pipe vs a pencil), not visual stimuli. Therefore it fails the review’s required inclusion criterion I3 (use of visual stimuli). The study does include a within-participant marijuana>control contrast (I4), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and cluster-corrected results (I5/I6), and provides participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software (I7). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Exclusion is based on not meeting I3.

This is an empirical task fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) in humans. It includes within-participant contrasts of natural reward cues > control (high-calorie food vs low-calorie food; food vs nonfood) and reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM12) acquired on a 3T scanner. Relevant study/sample information (participant ages, cue type, MRI field strength, processing software) are reported. Results are reported as whole-brain cluster-level findings (text/tables/figures). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual natural-reward cue-reactivity fMRI and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not non-empirical).

This study is an fMRI investigation of heroin cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts of heroin-related images > neutral images, presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (FDR-corrected) with regional coordinates and figures, and provides participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5). Although the paper also includes resting-state/graph-theory analyses, it additionally reports the required whole-brain task activation maps, so no exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual heroin cues with within-subject (heroin > neutral) contrasts and whole-brain, voxelwise SPM8 analyses on a 3.0 T scanner; however, the provided full text does not explicitly report participant sex/gender breakdown (the demographic details appear missing: “demographically matched ( )”), and therefore criterion I7 (relevant information reported regarding participant age and sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and processing software) is not fully satisfied. All other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Because at least one required inclusion criterion is not met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis based on the provided full text.

This fMRI study used visual cocaine-word cues and within-subject cocaine>neutral contrasts (I3, I4). However, all reported task activation analyses are ROI-based (small-volume corrections) and no unmasked group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) cocaine>neutral task activation map or whole-brain coordinates are reported in the main text (only ROI results and references to supplementary figures). Therefore it fails the requirement for a whole-brain task-evoked map and must be excluded under E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. The full text reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol > beverage and alcohol > visual control) and presents group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using SPM2 (random-effects t maps, p<.001, cluster threshold) with results summarized in tables/figures. Methods report MRI field strength (Philips 1.5 T) and processing software (SPM2), and participant demographics/sex/age information are presented (Table 1) along with cue type (alcohol). Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Full text is unavailable/truncated (site content failed to load). Although title and metadata indicate an fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity, the full article (methods, results) is not present, so I cannot verify required inclusion criteria: presence of a within-subject drug-cue>control contrast (I4), a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map (I5/I6), or reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software (I7). Because these core items cannot be confirmed from the incomplete record, the study cannot be included. Full text incompleteness prevents reliable assessment.

The full text reports an fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (color-word drug Stroop) in cocaine-dependent participants, with within-participant drug vs. matched neutral contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects t-tests and voxelwise regression/correlation maps are described and reported (voxelwise results and ROI confirmations), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps even though some drug>neutral contrasts did not reach cluster-corrected significance. Key methodological details are provided (participant ages/sex, cue type: cocaine, scanner field strength: 4T, processing software: SPM2). The article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting) apply.

This is an fMRI study of multisensory numeric Stroop (cognitive control) in recently abstinent cocaine users vs. controls. Although it uses whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports group differences, it does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, nor does it include any within-participant contrasts of drug-cues > control stimuli (or natural reward cues > control). Therefore it fails the review’s primary inclusion criteria (I3 and I4). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) but the experimental task is not a cue-reactivity paradigm. Exclusion is based on lack of cue-reactivity contrasts required for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cannabis cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The task included within-participant contrasts of cannabis vs. non-cannabis images and produced voxelwise whole-brain group-level statistical maps (thresholding and cluster-correction reported). The manuscript reports participant age/sex, cue type (cannabis), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). Whole-brain analyses were performed in addition to ROI analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol, neutral, abstract pictures) and adult alcohol-dependent participants. The study reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol vs neutral) and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded statistical maps reported and illustrated). Methods specify MRI field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (AFNI); participant demographics are referenced in Table 1 (demographic characteristics described in text). Thus all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without whole-brain task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study is an fMRI investigation of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using standardized visual pictorial stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts of smoking-related > neutral cues. It includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects, cluster-corrected Z-statistics) showing activation in several regions and reports coordinates and ROI analyses. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are all explicitly reported. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study comparing neural responses to cannabis cues, natural reward (fruit) cues, and neutral cues in long-term daily cannabis users and non-users. It includes within-participant contrasts (cannabis>neutral; cannabis>fruit; fruit>neutral), and reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (FEAT/FLAME) with corrected cluster thresholds. Visual stimuli were used (visual presentations of cannabis paraphernalia and fruit), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM8, FSL/FEAT) are reported. Demographic information is indicated in the methods and referenced tables (participants, exclusion criteria), and cue types and behavioral measures are described. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, meeting core content requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

Although this is an fMRI study of cocaine cue reactivity in regular users (visual drug cues implied) and reports participant age/sex and scanner field strength, the provided full text does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation results or coordinate tables/figures for the critical within-participant contrast (drug cues > control). Processing/analysis software is not reported in the main text (likely in supplementary material not provided). The main results focus on treatment (between-group) effects and ROIs; no unmasked whole-brain task maps or clear within-subject cue>control contrasts are available in the provided content, so the study cannot be included for the meta-analysis.

Full text is not accessible (website blocked / cookie notice); only title and bibliographic metadata are available. Cannot verify fundamental inclusion criteria: whether the study used functional MRI with visual drug cues (I3), included within-subject drug-cue>control contrasts (I4), reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (I5/I6), or provided required participant/scanner/software details (I7). The title suggests cue-processing and receptor measures, which may use PET rather than fMRI, but this cannot be confirmed without the full text. Because core eligibility cannot be assessed, exclude with low confidence and mark full text incomplete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (alcohol images vs soft drink images) with a within-subject contrast (alcohol blocks > soft drink blocks). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (exploratory whole-brain results with MNI coordinates and cluster-corrected p-values are provided). Relevant methodological details are reported: participant characteristics (all male, groups matched for age), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). The paper also reports ROI results but does not restrict itself to ROI-only analyses. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task map, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Accordingly, the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts of reward cues versus neutral cues and provides required methodological details (participants’ sex/age, scanner field strength, processing software), it does not assess drug cues or natural reward-related cues (e.g., food or sexual stimuli). The task used monetary incentive delay with geometric cues predicting monetary gain/loss, i.e., monetary reward anticipation rather than drug-cue or specified natural-reward cue-reactivity. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward-related cues>control). Whole-text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7. No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E3–E6) directly apply.

This study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug/food/sexual cues. It manipulates monetary reward contingencies during a counting Stroop task in cocaine-dependent and healthy control participants, not presentation of drug or natural reward cues (e.g., cocaine images vs control images). There is no within-participant contrast of drug-cue > control stimuli or natural-reward-cue > control stimuli, so I3 and I4 are not met. Although the paper reports participant demographics, scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM8) (satisfying I7), it does not meet the core cue-reactivity inclusion criteria required for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol>beverage; however, all reported analyses are ROI-based (predefined VS, mPFC, OFC) with no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain coordinates/figures reported. The meta-analysis requires at least one whole-brain group-level task activation map (or equivalent coordinate table/figure/supplement). Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Exclusion is based on E3 (only ROI analyses; no whole-brain results).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking-related vs. neutral images, and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with peak coordinates and statistical maps (p<0.001 uncorrected). Relevant methodological details are provided: participant sex/age information, cue type (nicotine/smoking-related visuals), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM5). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This study used fMRI with visual images of high-calorie foods (natural reward cues) and includes within-subject contrasts comparing high-calorie food images to matched non-food control images. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise exploratory analyses were performed and reported (p < .001) with coordinates and tables (e.g., right cerebellum, Table 1), in addition to ROI analyses. Key methodological details are reported (participant age and sex, cue type = food, 3T scanner field strength, processing software = SPM99). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-subject task activation maps; empirical human fMRI data).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity that uses visual stimuli. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs control pictures/odors and habituation terms) and examines pre- and post-treatment differences, and group-level mixed-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Z-scores, cluster-wise FWE correction). Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, alcohol cue type, 3T scanner, FSL processing). Results are reported as whole-brain task-evoked maps and described in the text with statistical thresholds and cluster-level inference. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes whole-brain task effects, empirical human fMRI data). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues with within-subject contrasts (heroin-related vs. neutral) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects, paired t-tests). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM2) are reported. Results include whole-brain activations presented in text/tables/coordinates. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used olfactory (ethanol odor) cues rather than visual stimuli. Inclusion criterion I3 requires fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli; therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria. The study does meet I4 (within-subject ethanol>neutral contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM results), I6 (whole-brain results reported in maps/tables), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type=alcohol, scanner field strength=1.5T, and processing software SPM reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts (smoking vs control) and reports participant demographics and scanner/processing details. However, the study reports ROI-based analyses (mean ROI responses and repeated-measures ANOVAs) rather than group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps. No unmasked whole-brain statistical maps or voxelwise results are provided, so it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study used resting-state fMRI to assess functional connectivity in smokers and did not employ a task-based cue-reactivity paradigm with visual stimuli. It contains no within-participant contrast of drug-cue > control-stimuli nor any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I3 or I4 and violates exclusion criterion E4 (resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, with within-subject contrasts (smoke vs rest/neutral) and group-level whole-brain random effects analyses (smoke cue vs rest) reported in the text and figures. Scanner field strength (3T), processing software (SPM8), participant age and sex, and cue type (nicotine/smoking images) are provided. The paper includes methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cocaine-related stimuli. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (Cocaine > Neutral) at the first level and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses. Whole-brain analyses and voxel coordinates are reported (including exploratory whole-brain results and specific MNI coordinates for group effects), and ROI analyses are complemented by small-volume corrections; processing details (SPM8) and MR field strength (3.0 T) are provided. Participant information and demographics are described (groups matched on age and sex), and cue type is cocaine. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol vs non-alcohol beverage images) with an explicit within-subject ALC>BEV (ALC-BEV) contrast. Analyses were conducted as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLMs with cluster-level FWE correction and reported cluster coordinates and figures. Methods report participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task map, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of cue reactivity to cannabis using visual stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts (cannabis vs. neutral) with coordinate tables and ROI results. However, the reported analyses are ROI-focused with small-volume FWE corrections and Bonferroni correction across a priori ROIs; no unambiguous whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (or whole-brain cluster-corrected results) are presented. Because the paper appears to report only ROI analyses without accompanying whole-brain task maps, it fails the whole-brain reporting requirement and meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because the fMRI cue modality during imaging was olfactory (alcohol aromas) rather than visual stimuli. The meta-analysis specifically requires studies that assess cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3). Although the study meets several other inclusion criteria (within-participant AO>ApCO contrast; whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with reported peaks/figures; and adequate reporting of participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software), the primary inclusion criterion I3 is not satisfied, so the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of alexithymia and insula/vmPFC functional connectivity in smokers versus nonsmokers. It does not include any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm using visual stimuli, nor any within-participant contrasts of drug-cues > control stimuli. The analyses are seed-based resting-state functional connectivity and mediation of trait→state relations, not task-evoked whole-brain activation maps. Therefore it fails to meet key inclusion criteria for a cue-reactivity meta-analysis (I3–I5) and fits exclusion criterion E4 (studies reporting only seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an event-related 3T fMRI study using visual cues (game screenshots and smoking images) and reports within-participant contrasts (gaming>neutral and smoking>neutral). Group-level, random-effects whole-brain activation maps for each group were obtained (thresholded at p<0.05 FDR) and reported in the text (regions and BA values), and conjunction analyses identify common activations. Relevant metadata are provided (participant sex/age description, cue types including nicotine and gaming, scanner field strength 3T, and processing software SPM5). Thus it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity fMRI, within-subject contrasts, whole-brain group maps (reported in text/figures), and requisite participant and acquisition details.

This is an fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visually presented drug-related words (visual stimuli). The paper reports within-participant cocaine>neutral (drug cues vs control stimuli) contrasts and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group contrast maps with FWE correction). Relevant metadata are provided (participant age/sex reporting, cocaine cue type, 3T scanner field strength, and processing software CamBA/SPM). The study therefore satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an fMRI investigation of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related vs neutral images with within-subject contrasts (smoking>neutral). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group peak in mPFC with cluster-corrected p-value) and provides coordinate data and cluster information. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0T Siemens Trio), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue stimuli (water-related and drug-related pictures) in heroin users. It reports within-subject contrasts (Thirst vs Neutral and Drug vs Neutral) at the group level using voxelwise, whole-brain SPM2 second-level one-sample t-tests, and reports peak coordinates and cluster information. Participant age and sex, scanner field strength (1.5T), cue types (heroin, water), and processing software (SPM2) are provided. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using visual natural reward (food) cues and reports within-subject contrasts of high-calorie (natural reward) versus non-food control stimuli. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented (contrasts thresholded and corrected for whole-brain multiple comparisons) and described in the text and results tables/figures. Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual alcohol cues (alcoholic beverage pictures) and neutral/control images, reporting within-subject contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AFNI, 3T scanner). The methods describe generation of individual and group statistical maps, condition vs scrambled baseline contrasts, and whole-brain family-wise error correction; although the alcoholic>neutral contrast showed no significant treatment effect, whole-brain task-evoked maps were produced and reported. Participant age and sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength, and processing software are provided. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol pictures) with appetitive (food) and neutral (items) controls. It reports within-participant contrasts comparing alcohol cues > control stimuli and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using FSL (mixed-effects FLAME1, cluster-corrected z>2.3). Participant age/sex, cue types (alcohol, food, items), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are all reported. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Only the abstract is provided (full text is incomplete). The study appears to be an fMRI study using visual cues (heroin-puffing movie and sexual movie), so I3 is likely met. However, critical inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the abstract: there is no information confirming a within-participant contrast of drug cues>control (I4), no confirmation that group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps were reported (I5/I6), and participant details (age/sex), scanner field strength, and processing software are not reported (I7). Because the full text (methods/results) is unavailable, I cannot confirm all required inclusion criteria, so the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article.

While this is an fMRI study using visual alcohol cues and reports group-level whole-brain task analyses and necessary methodological details (scanner field strength, processing software, cue type, and participant demographics), it does not include a within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli (e.g., alcohol images > neutral images). Instead, the reported primary contrasts compare identical alcohol cue presentations across instructional/manipulation conditions (prayer vs. passive vs. news). The study lacks an unambiguous drug-cue > control-stimulus within-subject contrast required by inclusion criterion I4, so it cannot be included in a meta-analysis of cue-reactivity contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual photographic stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts of smoking vs control cues; participant age/sex, scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM99) are reported. However, all reported neuroimaging analyses are ROI-based and the authors explicitly state they did not perform a standard voxel-wise whole-brain analysis; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables from whole-brain analyses are provided. This violates inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Although this study includes human fMRI of visual alcohol-related and affective stimuli (I3), the full text does not clearly report a within-participant contrast of alcohol cues > control stimuli (I4) nor a clearly described unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for alcohol cue-reactivity (I5). The reported imaging results emphasize between-group (LY686017 vs placebo) differences in response to affective images and refer to figures/tables (Fig. 4, table S3) in supplementary material; it is unclear whether an unmasked whole-brain alcohol-cue>neutral contrast at the group level is provided. Therefore the paper fails the required within-subject cue>control contrast and/or clear whole-brain task activation reporting and must be excluded (E5). Full text appears complete for the main article (supplementary materials referenced but not essential to determine the absence of the required contrasts).

This is an fMRI study using visual substance-related cues (alcohol, marijuana, polydrug) and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses and coordinate results. However, it does not include the required within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (e.g., alcohol cues > neutral/control). The main reported contrasts are non-studied versus studied (repetition-priming) alcohol/drug cues, which reflect implicit memory effects rather than classic cue-reactivity contrasts against control stimuli. Additionally, key reporting elements required by the meta-analysis (explicit participant ages and MRI scanner field strength) are not provided in this full text (the paper refers to an accompanying main study for acquisition parameters). Because it fails to meet I4 and I7, it must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of visual smoking cues with within-subject SCs vs NCs contrasts and reports participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, all reported voxelwise results were restricted to an a priori fronto-limbic mask (WFU PickAtlas) rather than an unmasked, whole-brain group-level analysis. The meta-analysis requires whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps; studies reporting only region-restricted/ROI-masked results do not meet that requirement. Therefore the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion items.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward (food) cues with healthy adult female participants (ages reported). The within-subject contrast food vs. non-food (control) images is explicitly reported. The paper describes group-level whole-brain activation analyses to food vs. non-food images (reported in the Supplementary material), satisfying the whole-brain/map requirement (I5/I6). Relevant details are provided: participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). Although primary hypothesis testing used anatomical ROIs (NAcc, vmPFC), whole-brain results are performed and referenced. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual stimuli (pictures) of gambling (natural reward) and smoking (drug) cues, with within-subject contrasts (gambling>neutral; smoking>neutral). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (SPM2; cluster-level correction; coordinates and figures/tables provided). Relevant methodological details are reported (all-male sample, cue types, 3.0T scanner, SPM2 processing). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). It includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM8 with voxelwise thresholds and AlphaSim-corrected cluster sizes; results are reported as coordinates and figures. Participant age range and sex distribution are provided, scanner field strength (3T Philips Intera) and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking vs neutral cues (subject-specific smoking–neutral contrasts and pre/post comparisons), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded maps and reported peak coordinates/clusters for mOFC, NAc, ACC, etc.). The paper reports participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using visual alcohol cue videos (alcohol drinking scenes) with a within-subject contrast of alcohol cue vs mosaic control. Analyses used whole-brain voxelwise GLM and random-effects group analysis; results are reported as significant clusters (FDR-corrected) with coordinates/BA and figures/tables. Scanner field strength (1.5T), processing software (BrainVoyager), cue type (alcohol), and participant demographics are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues and matched neutral images; it reports within-subject drug cue > neutral contrasts and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (paired t-tests and whole-brain correlations) with cluster-corrected results and reported coordinates. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL) are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply.

Only the article abstract is provided (full text missing). The abstract does not provide sufficient information to confirm key inclusion criteria: it is unclear whether visual stimuli (I3) were explicitly used in the fMRI cue-reactivity task, whether at least one within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli was reported (I4), and whether group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables were reported (I5/I6). Required participant/sample details and MRI processing details are not reported in the abstract (I7). Because the full text is not available, these critical items cannot be verified; therefore the study cannot be included at this stage.

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with within-participant contrasts (food > non-food) and reports key methodological details (age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner, FSL processing), the group-level statistical analysis was conducted using a masked, ROI-based approach (a priori anatomical masks fed to FSL RANDOMISE). The paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of cigarette cue reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking videos/images) and reports within-participant contrasts and ROI-based PSC and seed-based FC analyses. However, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map for drug cues > control stimuli. The analyses are primarily ROI-based and seed-based functional connectivity maps; thus it reports connectivity/seed-based results without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain task activation map. This matches exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI drug-cue with visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast used in analyses), and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software reported). Because no whole-brain task activation map is presented, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts of food>control. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5 second-level analyses) with tables/figures of activations and statistical thresholds. Participant age and sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core content is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (symbols signaling impending chocolate milk vs tasteless solution). It includes within-subject contrasts (anticipation chocolate milk vs anticipation tasteless solution; chocolate milk receipt vs tasteless receipt). Group-level voxelwise analyses and whole-brain regression are reported (with SPM8 processing, 3T scanner), and results are presented as brain maps/tables (with small-volume correction for ROIs and whole-brain thresholding). Participant age range and sex matching are reported. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7, and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, employing within-subject Craving>Neutral contrasts and group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses. The paper reports voxelwise results (coordinates, cluster sizes) and contrasts for Craving>Neutral within groups and for Schizophrenia>Controls, specifies cue type (cigarette/nicotine), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It contains within-participant smoking>neutral contrasts and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (random-effects GLM and mixed-effects ANCOVA) with cluster correction. Methods report participant sex (women), age comparisons, cue type (smoking/nicotine), MRI field strength (Siemens Trio 3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX), satisfying reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual drug cue-reactivity.

This is an ASL fMRI study using cocaine-related videos, but its primary analyses are seed-based functional connectivity and wavelet transform coherence between amygdala and dorsal cingulate during an attempted craving-inhibition task. It does not report a within-participant task contrast of drug cues > control stimuli, nor does it present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map (only seed-based whole-brain regression/connectivity maps). Therefore it does not meet the requirement for a task-evoked whole-brain activation contrast and is excluded under E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study that assessed smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and explicitly computed the within-subject contrast smoking cues > neutral cues. Analyses were performed with a whole-brain random-effects GLM (voxelwise maps reported, with FDR correction for n-back task and whole-brain cue analyses described even where some effects did not survive correction). Scanner field strength (3T), processing software (BrainVoyager QX), cue type (smoking/nicotine), and participant sex (male-only; demographics reported in Table 1) are provided. Although some cue effects did not survive multiple-comparisons correction, the study nevertheless reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps, meeting the meta-analysis requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This study used rtfMRI neurofeedback targeting an individually-defined ACC ROI and reports primarily ROI-based percent signal change analyses and behavioral craving ratings. While it meets several inclusion elements (visual nicotine cues, within-participant contrasts of smoke vs rest/neutral, and reports participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, and software), the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or coordinate tables of whole-brain results. The analyses and results are restricted to ROI-based effects, and no unmasked, whole-brain task activation map is reported. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results) and cannot be included in a meta-analysis requiring whole-brain task activation maps.

This is an empirical fMRI study of heroin cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (heroin-related vs neutral pictures) and includes within-subject contrasts (heroin>neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (P<0.001 uncorrected) with tables/figures describing activated clusters (including PCC coordinates). Relevant participant details (age, sex: males only), cue type (heroin), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. Although the paper also includes resting-state connectivity analyses, task-based whole-brain activation maps are present, so no exclusion criteria are violated. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol (drug) cues and soft-drink control cues with an implicit approach-avoidance task. The study reports within-subject contrasts isolating alcohol-related cue-reactivity (interaction and component contrasts), performs second-level group voxelwise analyses, and indicates whole-brain analyses (Supplementary Table S1). Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol, soft-drink), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria.

The provided full text is incomplete—only title/metadata are available and the article content did not load. I cannot verify key inclusion criteria: whether visual smoking cues were used in the task, whether a within-participant drug-cue > control-stimuli contrast was reported, whether group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps (or coordinate tables clearly describing whole-brain results) are present, or whether participant age/sex, scanner field strength, and processing software were reported. Because these elements cannot be assessed from the available content, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria and is therefore excluded pending access to the complete full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a visual monetary incentive delay (MID) task (visual cue shapes signaling monetary rewards/loss-avoidance). It includes within-subject contrasts of reward anticipation versus non-incentive (reward>non-reward) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (voxelwise t-tests, familywise-corrected activations, tables/figures). Relevant participant and scanner metadata are provided (ages 12–16, sex counts, cue type: monetary reward, scanner field strength 3T, processing software AFNI). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and includes within-subject contrasts of smoking>neutral images. However, all reported neural analyses were performed using predefined region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (14 ROIs); the manuscript does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I7) are satisfied, but lack of whole-brain voxelwise results prevents inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Although this study includes an fMRI task (drug words) and within-subject contrasts (drug>fixation; drug>neutral words), the reported fMRI results are presented as ROI-extracted effects (OFC, ventral striatum) and composite/ROI analyses. The paper mentions testing whole-brain diagnosis×DAT1 interactions, but no whole-brain task-evoked, voxelwise activation maps or peak coordinates for the drug>control contrasts are reported in the text provided. Because the study does not provide a group-level whole-brain task activation map (or coordinates/figures describing such a map) for the drug>control contrast, it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results and therefore meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is a whole-brain fMRI study using visual cannabis cues (meets I3, I5, I6, I7). However, the primary reported analyses are an approach-bias contrast [(approach-cannabis + avoid-control) > (avoid-cannabis + approach-control)] and condition > baseline contrasts. The paper does not report a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (e.g., cannabis > control) as a group-level whole-brain task contrast, which fails inclusion criterion I4. Because all inclusion criteria must be met, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that used visual (and auditory) stimuli. Analyses include within-participant contrasts of food cues versus neutral nonfood control stimuli and high-ED versus low-ED food cues. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM5 with cluster-corrected results reported (tables/figures provided). Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine’s effects on working memory and chronic smoking (task-based WM with mixed block/event design). It does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, nor does it include within-participant contrasts of drug cues > control stimuli. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3 and I4). Although it reports whole-brain task activation maps and participant demographics, the primary objective and task do not match the review’s cue-reactivity requirement.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (drug-related words) and includes within-participant contrasts of drug vs. neutral words. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster- and voxel-level thresholds; tables/figures/coordinates provided), and supplementary ROI analyses are secondary. The manuscript provides participant demographics (age, sex distribution), cue type (cocaine drug words), MRI scanner field strength (4T), and processing software (SPM2). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core content is present. Therefore it meets all specified inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation of cue-reactivity using visual alcohol, marijuana, and polydrug picture stimuli in at-risk college students. It reports within-subject contrasts of substance-related cues > neutral cues, conducted as group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses using FSL, with results described in text, tables/figures (coordinates and images) and standard whole-brain thresholds. Participant age/sex, cue types, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria are met.

Although this is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity with within-subject alcohol>control contrasts and whole-brain group analyses (3T scanner, FSL), the primary alcohol cues were gustatory (taste delivery via gustometer), not visual images. The meta-analysis requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3); this study does not meet that criterion and therefore must be excluded. Other inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food). It includes within-subject contrasts of hedonic food cues > nonfood control stimuli, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and MNI coordinates. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

The provided full text is incomplete (only acknowledgments and references are present). The article title indicates an fMRI study of visual food cues in PCOS patients, so it likely addresses natural reward (food) cue-reactivity (I3). However, core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is missing, so I cannot verify critical inclusion criteria: whether a within-participant contrast of food cues>control was reported (I4), whether group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps were provided or reported (I5/I6), or whether participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software were reported (I7). Because essential information is absent, the study cannot be confirmed eligible and is excluded pending availability of the complete full text.

This study is a resting-state seed-based functional connectivity (habenula–striatum) analysis comparing opioid-using versus non-using psychiatric inpatients. It does not involve a task-based cue-reactivity paradigm, nor any presentation of visual drug or natural reward cues. No within-participant task contrast (e.g., drug cues > control stimuli) or task-evoked whole-brain (voxelwise) activation maps are reported. Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria requiring task-based fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and whole-brain task maps. Exclusion is based on reporting only resting-state/seed-based connectivity and ROI-focused analyses without whole-brain task activation.

Although this fMRI study used visual cues (images of money and cigarette puffs) and within-subject contrasts (money>neutral; puff>neutral) and reported participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software, the analyses and reported results focus on a priori ROI-derived striatal clusters and extracted eigenvariates. The manuscript does not present or describe an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the cue>control contrasts; results are reported as ROI findings. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence and meets Exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, reporting within-subject contrasts (alcohol > neutral) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses performed in SPM (SPM5/SPM8) on data acquired at 3T. Whole-brain activation results are described (and illustrated) in the text and used in subsequent ROI/correlation and Cox regression analyses. Relevant participant information (age range, sex/gender representation discussion), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software are reported. The paper is empirical, not solely ROI- or connectivity-based, and provides task-evoked whole-brain maps/analyses, satisfying inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task analyses (2×2 ANOVA and smoking–neutral contrast) with cluster-wise correction and presents whole-brain results/maps. Imaging details and processing software are reported (3.0T Philips scanner; AFNI). Participant characteristics (male adult smokers, n=32; descriptive statistics referenced) and cue type are provided. The study also reports additional connectivity analyses, but critically includes whole-brain task-evoked activation maps, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This study is an fMRI investigation of practice/habituation effects on a sustained attention task with monetary incentives, not a visual cue-reactivity study. It does not present any within-participant contrasts comparing drug-related or natural reward-related visual cues versus control stimuli (no drug-cue > control or food/sexual cue contrasts). Although whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses are reported (and participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software are described), the key eligibility for this meta-analysis (I3/I4) is not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis of visual drug/natural reward cue-reactivity.

Full text is unavailable/incomplete (page failed to load). Title/metadata suggest an fMRI study of cocaine cue reactivity, but core article content (methods, results) is missing, so I cannot verify key inclusion criteria: use of visual stimuli, presence of within-participant drug cue>control contrasts, whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, and reporting of participant and MRI details. Because these cannot be confirmed from the provided content, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis until the full text is obtained.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with a within-subject contrast (appetitive > neutral) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses. The paper reports brain activation maps/clusters (with voxelwise thresholds and cluster sizes) and provides necessary methodological details (participant sex and age comparisons, cue type: food, 3T scanner, BrainVoyager processing). Results include coordinates/regions and statistical values and correlations. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Limitations, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s requirement for cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3). The experimental cues were verbal warning cues signaling intravenous nicotine or saline infusion (anticipation of infusion), not visual drug-related cues; although neutral IAPS slides were shown to reduce boredom, the critical cue manipulation was verbal/infusion-based. In addition, the fMRI analyses were focused on a priori anatomical regions using averaged percent signal change within masks (ROI/masked analyses) rather than reporting an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map, triggering exclusion under E3. While the study does include a within-participant contrast (nicotine vs saline anticipation) and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software (satisfying I4 and I7), failure to use visual cue-reactivity and lack of whole-brain voxelwise task maps mean key inclusion criteria (I3 and I5) are not met.

Although the study uses an fMRI reward-cue antisaccade task with visual monetary cues (reward vs neutral) and reports within-subject reward>neutral contrasts and adequate methodological details (age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner, FSL), the paper only reports ROI-based results. The authors state whole-brain analyses were run but no whole-brain clusters were identified beyond a priori ROIs, and they report only ROI results. This meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only reporting with no whole-brain results). Therefore it does not satisfy the meta-analysis requirement for a reported group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map (I5). Full text appears complete.

This study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue reactivity using visual drug/natural reward cues. It uses a reinforcement-learning task with abstract stimuli and reward/punishment feedback (smiling/frowning faces), not drug or food cues; therefore inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are not met. Although the study reports whole-brain task-evoked fMRI maps (satisfying I5/I6) and reports participant demographics (I7), the core requirement of cue-reactivity contrasts (drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward cues > control) is absent. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity that reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral control stimuli and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (tables of coordinates and figures). Participant characteristics are reported (Table 1) and fMRI acquisition/analysis details are provided in the paper (with further details in supplementary material), satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without a whole-brain task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

Although this fMRI study used visual alcohol and food cues and reports whole-brain task activation maps (win>lose) with coordinates, it does NOT report a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (no alcohol>neutral or food>neutral task-evoked contrast is presented). The main analyses focus on monetary reward (win vs lose) and personal-reference (high vs low) contrasts; stimulus-category effects are tested but no unmasked, whole-brain cue-reactivity contrast for alcohol or food is reported. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met, so the study cannot be included in the meta-analysis. Relevant inclusion criteria that are met: I3, I5, I6, I7. Relevant exclusion criterion: E5 (no accompanying whole-brain task effect for cue-reactivity). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of food versus control pictures, and group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses conducted in SPM5 with results described in text/tables/figures. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening.

The study is an fMRI investigation of responses to food images and meets several inclusion items: it uses visual natural reward cues (food) (I3), includes within-participant contrasts of appetizing food > control stimuli (I4), and reports group-level whole-brain analyses for task contrasts (I5) with results described in text/figures/supplement (I6). However, the provided full-text is incomplete with regard to participant demographic details: ages and sex are not explicitly reported in the supplied content (they are referenced as being given in tables not included here). Inclusion criterion I7 (reporting participant age and sex) cannot be verified from the provided extract. Because not all inclusion criteria can be confirmed and key participant information is missing, I mark the full text as incomplete and exclude the study pending retrieval of the complete article (or supplemental tables) to confirm I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food stimuli. It reports within-subject food>nonfood contrasts, presents voxel-wise (whole-brain) task-evoked results (figures and MNI coordinates for local maxima), and describes processing/software (AFNI), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and participant age/sex. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual reward-predicting cues (money and cigarettes) and an event-related design. The authors performed within-subject contrasts of anticipation to reward-predicting stimuli (parametric increase across reward levels, including 0/no-reward trials) for cigarette and monetary cues, enabling drug-cue>control and natural-reward>control contrasts. Analyses were conducted as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM5 analyses with reported whole-brain results (thresholding described, clusters and peak coordinates referenced), and MRI field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM5) are specified. Participant demographics (age and sex) are reported in the paper’s subject data/tables (referenced in the text). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (movie clips). The authors report within-participant contrasts of smoking scenes > matched nonsmoking control scenes and performed group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (voxelwise maps reported with coordinates, figures, and tables). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with within-subject task contrasts (high-calorie/low-calorie/non-food regressors) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected results reported and shown in figures/tables). Participant age and sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (BioImageSuite/AFNI pipeline) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete and meets all required inclusion criteria.

This study reports resting-state fMRI effects of an acute pharmacological intervention (KB220Z) in abstinent heroin users using a randomized crossover design. It does not assess cue-reactivity to visual drug or natural reward stimuli, and there is no within-participant task contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli. Analyses are resting-state/MVPA and ROI/connectivity-oriented rather than task-evoked whole-brain maps of visual cue-reactivity. Therefore it does not meet the review’s core inclusion criteria for task-based visual cue-reactivity fMRI.

This is a within-subject fMRI study of smokers using visual smoking videos versus neutral videos, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported. Methods report scanner field strength (3 T), processing software (fmristat), participant ages and sex, and contrasts of smoking>neutral were analyzed and reported with whole-brain results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study does not investigate drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug/food/sexual cues. It is an fMRI study of aversive (fear) conditioning and extinction using colored squares paired with an electrical shock (CS+ vs CS−), i.e., threat-related cues rather than drug or natural reward cues. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I3 (must assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli). Although it reports whole-brain task-evoked fMRI results and participant details (methods, scanner, analyses), the stimulus domain and task do not match the meta-analysis objective. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with an explicit within-participant contrast of food>scrambled control images. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task effects (food vs. control) and voxelwise results (main effect of task and correlations), provides coordinate tables and SPM analyses, and reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with a within-participant contrast of high-calorie (HC) vs low-calorie (LC) food cues. Whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses were reported (repeated-measures ANOVAs with cluster-level FWE correction) using SPM12 on a 3T scanner. Participant demographic information (age, sex) and cue type (food) are provided. The study also reports additional connectivity (PPI) analyses, but crucially includes unmasked whole-brain task activation maps/analyses rather than only ROI or connectivity results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol-related cues (images) with age- and sex-reported participant groups. It reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol-related > non-alcoholic beverage control stimuli (alcohol-beverage), and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AFNI; voxel-wise thresholds and cluster reporting) with tables/coordinates and supplementary materials. Scanner field strength (1.5T), cue type (alcohol), and processing software (AFNI) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes whole-brain task effects). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is a protocol/design paper for a randomized controlled trial that describes planned fMRI procedures but reports no original task-evoked fMRI data or group-level whole-brain statistical maps. Additionally, the cue paradigm uses personalized auditory imagery scripts (audio cues) rather than visual stimuli, so it does not meet the requirement for cue-reactivity with visual stimuli. Therefore it does not provide the within-participant drug-cue>control visual contrast maps or whole-brain task activation maps required for inclusion. Exclusion is based primarily on E6 (non-empirical/protocol paper without original human fMRI results). It also fails I3 (visual-stimulus cue modality) and I5/I4 (no reported within-subject cue>control whole-brain maps or analyses).

The full text reports an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study in alcohol-dependent patients using visual alcohol images, with within-subject contrasts (alcohol>neutral). The paper includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain thresholds and reported clusters/coordinates) in addition to ROI tests. Key methodological details are reported (participant sex/age range, cue type = alcohol, 3-T scanner, SPM5/8 preprocessing), satisfying reporting requirements. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-subject task activation maps).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (novel geometric CS) experimentally paired with alcohol in human heavy drinkers. The paper reports within-participant contrasts between CS+ (alcohol-paired) and CS− (saline-paired), including whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected cluster statistics and tables/figures of activation (satisfying whole-brain reporting). Subject characteristics (age, sex), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. Although the primary reported effect was CS−>CS+ (i.e., CS+ produced negative BOLD), a within-subject CS+ vs CS− task contrast was performed and examined. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion presented.

This fMRI study investigates cue-reactivity to a natural reward (chocolate) using visual stimuli (pictures of dark vs. white chocolate) and flavored delivery, includes within-participant contrasts comparing chocolate-related visual cues to a grey control and other control stimuli, and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2) with cluster and small-volume-corrected results and stereotactic coordinates. Participant demographics (age range 20–30, all female), cue type (food/chocolate), scanner field strength (3.0 T) and processing software (SPM2) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting) apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s core inclusion criteria. It is a PET molecular imaging study measuring mu-opioid receptor binding and treatment outcome, not an fMRI task study of cue-reactivity using visual drug/natural reward cues. There is no within-participant task contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli, no task-evoked fMRI whole-brain activation maps, and no visual cue-reactivity paradigm. Although the full text is complete and reports participant demographics and voxelwise PET (SPM) analyses, these do not satisfy I3 (fMRI), I4 (within-participant cue>control task contrast), or I5 (task-evoked whole-brain fMRI activation map).

This study is an rTMS clinical trial that used structural MRI for neuronavigation but did not acquire or report task-based functional MRI activation maps. It does not assess fMRI cue-reactivity or report any within-participant drug-cue > control whole-brain contrasts. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity (I3 and I4) and provides no whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or coordinates (I5/I6). The full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on absence of task-based fMRI cue-reactivity data rather than on non-empirical status.

This is an fMRI study of emotional (negative face) processing and its correlation with cigarette use, not a cue-reactivity task using drug- or natural-reward-related visual cues. It therefore fails inclusion criterion I3 (not assessing drug/natural reward cue-reactivity). Additionally, the reported analyses are ROI-based insula extractions and correlations; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps for drug/natural cue>control are reported, invoking exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation that used visual drug cues (photographs of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages) and included within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > control stimuli. The methods describe group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps (voxel-wise t-tests of β-coefficients) and present at least one whole-brain task-evoked map (fearful vs neutral faces) using AFNI on a 3T scanner. Participant demographics (age range, sex) and cue type are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This study is not a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual drug or natural reward cues. It reports arterial spin labeling (CBF) measurements during rest and a spatial working-memory task in abstinent alcoholic men, with no presentation of drug/food/sexual cues and no within-participant contrast of drug-cue > control stimuli. While whole-brain CBF maps are reported for rest and working-memory conditions, these are not cue-reactivity task-evoked maps required by the review. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I7. The full text appears complete.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures) with within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs neutral/abstract) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with coordinates and cluster results. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The manuscript includes full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore it meets all stated inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate listed exclusion criteria.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual cues (alcohol-associated pictures and IAPS positive/negative pictures) and reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol>neutral, positive>neutral, negative>neutral). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (SPM5; thresholding and tables/figures referenced). Key participant details (age, sex), cue types, scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues in chronic smokers. It reports within-subject contrasts of aversive smoking-related > neutral and appetitive smoking-related > neutral, and group-level random-effects whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (SPM5) with cluster correction (AFNI 3dClustSim). Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0 T) and processing software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI visual cue-reactivity studies and provides whole-brain results reported in the text/tables.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking > neutral cues and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (FLAME, cluster-corrected) for the smoking vs. neutral contrast. Relevant methodological and participant details are provided (age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, FSL processing). The whole-brain results are described in the text and compared to a DMN ROI; beta-weights were extracted and correlated with MRS measures. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study using a monetary incentive delay task (visual cues signaling potential monetary reward), i.e., natural reward-related visual stimuli. The analyses include within-participant contrasts of gain versus nongain (reward-related cues > control), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FWE-corrected and less stringent whole-brain results). Results are reported in text/tables and ROI/whole-brain analyses; processing software (SPM2) and participant demographics (matched on age and gender) are provided. These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for cue type, within-subject contrasts, whole-brain maps (reported), and reporting format. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual methamphetamine and sexual images in human participants (men aged 19–45). It reports within-subject contrasts (methamphetamine>neutral; sexual>neutral and sexual>methamphetamine) and group-level mixed-effects analyses. The paper includes whole-brain, voxelwise results (cluster peak coordinates, F-statistic, cluster size, and p-value for the left superior frontal cortex), and describes whole-brain correction thresholds and SPM12 processing on a 3.0-T scanner. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, scanner field strength, and processing software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The study does not meet the key inclusion criterion I3 because cue-reactivity was elicited using gustatory (taste) stimuli delivered via a gustometer (alcohol vs lychee juice), not visual stimuli.
