It does meet several other inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant alcohol>control contrast), I5/I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps reported and corrected; results described in text/tables/figures), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type [alcohol], scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [FSL, FreeSurfer] reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are triggered. Because the meta-analysis specifically requires visual cue paradigms (I3), this study must be excluded.

The study is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject first-level contrasts (alcohol > neutral) and second-level, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5/8) with cluster-wise FWE correction; results are presented in tables and figures. Participant age range and sex distribution, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T MAGNETOM Trio), and processing software (SPM5/8) are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

The article is a behavioral/psychological study assessing urge to drink using personalized in vivo and videotaped alcohol cues; the abstract and available text describe self-report craving measures and no fMRI data, imaging methods, or neuroimaging results. Therefore it does not meet I3 (not a functional MRI study) and lacks whole-brain task-evoked maps required by I5. Other required items for inclusion (I4 within-participant fMRI contrasts, I7 reporting of scanner field strength and processing software) are not present. The provided content appears to be only abstract/metadata rather than the complete article text, so fulltext_incomplete is set to true. Closest applicable exclusion criterion: study does not report original human fMRI data (E6).

The provided content is only a brief summary/abstract, not the full text. The summary confirms this is an fMRI study presenting alcohol-related visual stimuli (meets I3). However, core methodological and result details necessary to confirm all inclusion criteria are missing: I4 (explicit within-participant drug-cue > control contrast) and I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps) cannot be verified from the summary; I7 (participant age/sex, scanner field strength, and processing software) is not reported. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and these cannot be confirmed, the study must be excluded pending full-text review. It is also unclear whether the study reports only ROI or between-group contrasts (potential exclusions E3/E5), so obtain the full text for reassessment.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast. Group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results are reported (cluster-corrected maps and tables), and results are described in the text and figures. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type is nicotine, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL) are specified. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are applicable.

This is a PET study (H2(15)O PET) rather than an fMRI study, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I3 (Functional MRI study assessing cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). The full text is complete and the study does meet several other inclusion criteria (within-participant contrast of drug video > neutral video; group-level voxelwise whole-brain SPM results; results reported in text/figures/tables; participant age/sex/cue type and processing software reported), but failure to satisfy I3 is sufficient for exclusion. No exclusion criteria from the review’s list specifically apply (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical), so exclusion is based on modality mismatch.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking stimuli (meets I3) with a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast (meets I4) and reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software (meets I7). However, the paper’s analyses are focused on a priori ROI sphere analyses (average beta values extracted from 4 mm spheres) and subsequent Cox/logistic regressions; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps, coordinates, or whole-brain results are reported for the task contrast. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and qualifies for exclusion under E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete. Excluded on E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking-related images) with a within-participant contrast (smoking > neutral). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (cluster-corrected) comparing smoking vs neutral images and further reports ROI and ICA results. Key methodological details required by the review are present: cue type (nicotine), participant sex (women only), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). The whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/results are described in the text and corrected for multiple comparisons. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This study is an fMRI investigation of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using audio-visual (visual) smoking cues and a within-subject contrast of smoking cues > non-smoking cues. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM8) with reported voxel coordinates and cluster-corrected results; MRI field strength (3.0T), participant age/sex, cue type, and processing software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and does not violate exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high- vs low-caloric food images). It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., high-caloric > low-caloric in Tea and Water conditions and interaction contrasts) and conducted exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analyses and ROI analyses; whole-brain results are described in text and supplementary materials. Participant age/sex (young adult women), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The paper is an empirical fMRI study of non-drug (monetary) reward-related cue processing using visual cues. It reports within-subject contrasts of reward-related cues versus nonreward controls (pre-response $1/$10 vs $0; WIN vs HIT cues; reward notification contrasts). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps were computed and reported (AFNI 3dMEMA; FDR-corrected maps, tables and figures). Participant age/sex, cue type (monetary), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual cigarette images (meets I3 and I4; participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and software are reported meeting I7). However, all primary statistical tests reported are region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (a priori anatomically defined ROIs and ROI-based hypothesis testing). The manuscript does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables/figures of whole-brain results. Therefore it reports only ROI results with no whole-brain activation map, violating inclusion criterion I5 and meeting exclusion criterion E3.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of visual natural reward (food) cue reactivity in humans. It reports within-subject contrasts of food vs. non-food (control) stimuli, performs group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses using FSL/FLAME1 with cluster correction and presents whole-brain results in figures/tables. Participant age, sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task map, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual food images (a natural reward) and reports within-subject contrasts comparing craved food cues to control stimuli (Look Craved > Look Not Craved; Look Craved > Look Neutral). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected results and peak coordinates), with processing details (SPM12b, AFNI/AlphaSim), scanner field strength (3.0 T Siemens Skyra), and participant demographics (ages 10–23, all female) provided. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity (I3, I4) and the requirements for whole-brain reporting and methodological details (I5–I7). No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical BOLD-fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of food vs. non-food control stimuli, and includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR cluster-corrected) in addition to ROI analyses. The paper provides participant age and sex, cue type (food), MRI scanner details (MAGNETOM Prisma, methods note optimization at 3T), and processing software (FSL). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking-related and affective cues and reports within-subject contrasts (smoking>neutral, positive>neutral), and reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, all group-level statistical testing was conducted within an a priori anatomical mask (an inclusive AAL ROI mask) rather than as an unmasked whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map. Because the paper reports only masked/ROI-constrained voxelwise results (i.e., no unmasked whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), it does not meet the review’s whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and thus falls under exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so exclusion is based on analytic approach rather than missing information.

The study does not meet I3: it is not an fMRI study of drug cues or of the natural reward cue types specified for the review (e.g., food or sexual cues). The fMRI component used monetary reward cues (secondary reinforcer) in an incentive-conflict task rather than drug-related cues or the natural reward types targeted by the meta-analysis. The paper does, however, include within-participant contrasts of rewarded vs nonrewarded stimuli (meets I4), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps (meets I5), and presents coordinate-based results/whole-brain activations (meets I6). Reporting of participant demographics and some methodological details is present but the cue type (monetary) falls outside the review’s defined cue domains. Because I3 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded per the protocol.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (beverage pictures paired with IAPS images). The authors report within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol versus non-alcohol beverage cues (e.g., alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage cues paired with negative and positive images), and present group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (voxel-wise t-tests with cluster correction) described in text, tables and figures. Relevant methodological details are reported: participant sex (all male, age-matched groups), scanner field strength (3-T), and processing software (AFNI). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Full text is not accessible (site content failed to load). Only title/metadata are available; core article content (methods, results) cannot be reviewed. Cannot confirm critical inclusion criteria: whether this is an fMRI task with within-participant drug-cue>control contrasts (I4), and crucially whether group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables are reported (I5/I6). Participant details and MRI/processing parameters (I7) also cannot be verified. Because essential information is missing, the study cannot be reliably assessed for inclusion in the meta-analysis and is excluded pending retrieval of the full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study of appetitive (natural food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (pictures) with within-subject contrasts (CS+ vs CS−) reported during an fMRI reinstatement test. Group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses were conducted (flexible factorial model) and whole-brain results/coordinates are reported (MNI peaks given; exploratory whole-brain maps described). Relevant details are provided: participant age/sex, cue type (food), 3T scanner field strength, and processing software (SPM12). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (AAT alcohol vs soft drink images) in human participants. It reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol cues to control stimuli (e.g., [alcohol pull > soft drink pull]) and other alcohol>control contrasts. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (including whole-brain results and peak coordinates; small-volume and whole-brain FWE-corrected results are described); preprocessing and analysis software (SPM8) and scanner field strength (3T) are provided, and participant sex (male) and demographic matching are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3–I7) and does not violate exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of visual food-cue reactivity (natural reward) and includes within-subject contrasts of food vs. object stimuli, but the fMRI analyses and results are reported as ROI-based COPE extractions and ROI-wise mixed-effects models. The paper does not present or describe any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps, nor tables of whole-brain coordinates or whole-brain figures; therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study uses individualized script-driven imagery (auditory/internal imagery) rather than visual stimuli. The meta-analysis inclusion criterion I3 requires fMRI cue-reactivity studies using visual stimuli; this is not met. The full text is complete and the study does meet other criteria (within-participant cue>control contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise analyses, appropriate reporting of participant details and processing), but failure to use visual cue stimuli precludes inclusion.

This paper reports a behavioral cue-reactivity experiment using self-report craving and mood measures in alcoholics; no fMRI or neuroimaging methods, analyses, or whole-brain activation maps are described. Therefore it does not meet the primary inclusion criterion I3 (functional MRI study using visual stimuli). Consequently I4–I7 are not satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is an empirical pupillometry (eye-tracking) study of cue-reactivity in alcohol-dependent patients and does not use functional MRI. It therefore fails the primary inclusion criterion I3 (must be an fMRI study). Consequently it cannot satisfy I4–I7 (within-subject fMRI contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise maps, MRI scanner/processing details). Full text appears complete. No fMRI data, whole-brain results, or MRI methods are reported, so the study is not eligible for a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity.

This article is a symposium/review summarizing multiple human laboratory studies (IV alcohol self-administration, cortisol/ACTH, clinical data) rather than reporting an original task-based fMRI experiment with visual drug/natural reward cues. The text does not present a within-participant contrast of drug-cues>control with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables required for inclusion. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical/review without original human fMRI data). The full text appears complete.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual drug (cigarette) and natural-reward (food) cues with whole-brain analyses reported, it does not include a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control (neutral) stimuli or natural reward cues > control stimuli. The task contrasts cognitive regulation (LATER vs NOW) and compares cigarette vs food cues, but no neutral control stimulus contrast (e.g., drug>neutral) is reported. Therefore Inclusion Criterion I4 is not met. Additionally, the manuscript does not explicitly report MRI scanner field strength (Tesla) required by I7, though scanner model and processing software (SPM5) are provided. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This article is a narrative review summarizing prior fMRI and MRS studies of various drugs rather than an original empirical fMRI study. The full text presents summary findings and references but does not report new human fMRI data, nor does it present within-participant drug-cues>control contrasts, group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps, or coordinate tables from an original experiment. Therefore it meets the exclusion criterion for non-empirical papers and does not satisfy the inclusion criteria for empirical cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This study is a resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity comparison between alcohol dependence and internet gaming disorder, not a task-based cue-reactivity fMRI study using visual drug or natural reward cues. It does not include any within-participant contrasts of drug-cue > control stimuli or a task-evoked whole-brain activation map. Therefore it violates the review’s inclusion requirements and meets exclusion criteria for resting-state/seed-based studies without task activation and for reporting only group comparisons without an unmasked whole-brain task effect.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food) and reports group-level whole-brain analyses with sufficient participant and scanner details, it does not include a within-participant contrast of reward cues versus an independent control stimulus (e.g., non-reward/neutral images). The reported contrasts compare cognitive strategies (up-regulation, suppression, reappraisal) and passive viewing of the same food images rather than food cues > control-stimuli contrasts required by the meta-analysis (I4). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4 and must be excluded.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (International Smoking Image Series). It reports within-subject contrasts (smoking cues > neutral cues) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected results reported; smoking vs. neutral activations in smokers, interaction effects). Methods and results are reported across Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and include participant age and sex (young male smokers and matched nonsmokers), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8, FSL). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text appears complete (contains methods, results, figures, and discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Although this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of alcohol with appropriate within-subject alcohol>control contrasts, whole-brain group analyses, and reported participant demographics and processing details, it uses gustatory (taste) cues (alcohol taste vs litchi) rather than visual stimuli. The meta-analysis specifically requires visual-stimulus cue-reactivity studies (I3). Because the cue modality does not meet I3, the study must be excluded. All other relevant inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied.

This is an empirical fMRI (and EEG) study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking vs neutral pictures and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected maps and tables of activations). Cue type, participant demographics (age/sex distribution), and task details are reported; additional methodological details (acquisition/preprocessing) are provided in the Supporting Information. The study therefore meets the meta-analysis requirements for task-based, whole-brain fMRI cue-reactivity data.

This is an fMRI study of real smoking decisions with stress manipulations and in-scanner e-cigarette puffs, not a visual cue-reactivity paradigm. Although whole-brain analyses are reported and participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and analysis software (AFNI) are provided, the task does not present drug-related visual cues nor report a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli. Thus it fails the core inclusion requirements for cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3 and I4). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Exclusion is based on not meeting required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis scope.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cues and includes within-participant contrasts (fattening > nonfattening) and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL, FreeSurfer, AFNI), satisfying I3, I4, and I7. However, the paper uses an a priori ROI approach and reports ROI/global-average and ROI-specific results. There is no clear report of an unmasked, group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or coordinates for whole-brain results; analyses and results are ROI-focused. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study (study 1) that probes neural cue-reactivity to palatable food using visual cues (milkshake image) and tastant delivery. It includes within-participant contrasts (anticipatory food cue > anticipatory tasteless-solution cue and receipt contrasts), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-level q-FDR corrected) with peak coordinates and effect sizes. Methods report participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (Siemens Allegra 3T), and processing software (SPM12). Full article text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (food) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and adequate reporting of age/sex, scanner field strength and processing software, it does not include a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control stimuli (e.g., food images > neutral/non-food images). The reported contrasts compare task instructions applied to the same food cues (inhibition vs. passive viewing, imaginary eating vs. passive viewing) rather than cue versus neutral/control stimuli. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4 and cannot be included in a meta-analysis requiring reward-cue > control stimulus contrasts. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food) with within-subject contrasts (high-calorie foods>objects; low-calorie foods>objects). Group-level second-level random-effects analyses were performed; authors state they conducted whole-brain analyses (reported at P<0.001 FWE-corrected) in addition to ROI small-volume corrections. Relevant participant information (female, ages 19–28), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI studies and no exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of smokers using visual pictorial smoking cues and neutral controls. It reports within-subject contrasts contrasting smoking vs neutral pictures (LCSP minus LCNP) and a cue-exposure-corrected attention contrast, and conducts group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise analyses with coordinates and Z-values. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3,I4,I5,I6,and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of amphetamine-related cue reactivity using visual stimuli (drug-related films). It reports a within-subject Drug movies > Neutral movies contrast and group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results with FWE correction; processing software (SPM12), scanner field strength (3T), participant age and sex are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual stimuli (images of palatable foods) to probe natural reward-related cue-reactivity in adolescents. The design includes within-participant contrasts (palatable vs non-palatable and palatable vs neutral) and group-level, whole-brain, voxel-wise analyses (ANOVA and second-level mixed-effects models) using SPM8 on a 3.0T scanner. Relevant participant information (age group: adolescents) and cue type (food) are reported. Although some between-group voxel-wise results did not survive multiple-comparison correction and some activation contrasts are not fully reported in the text, whole-brain analyses were performed and described. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual smoking-related video cues (nicotine cue), with within-subject contrasts of smoking videos > control videos. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (FLAME 1) with permutation-based TFCE correction and presents whole-brain results in text, figures and supplementary table. Participant age and sex are provided, cue type is nicotine, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are violated.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual Pavlovian cues (colored lights and snack images) associated with food rewards (natural rewards). The study includes within-subject contrasts comparing cue types (e.g., CS+ > CS− and specific PIT contrasts) that reflect cue-evoked activation, reports whole-brain group-level analyses (with results and a NeuroVault collection of maps), and provides participant demographics, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity and provides whole-brain task-evoked maps/results.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of cigarette (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (dynamic videos). It includes within-participant contrasts of smoking > neutral cues, reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (peak coordinates and z-statistics reported), and provides necessary methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, and FSL processing). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural-reward (food) cues with a within-subject contrast of food>neutral. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results (1-sample t test of food>neutral, FWE-corrected clusters shown and described), uses SPM5 for processing, and specifies participant age/sex, cue type (food), and scanner field strength (3T). Figures and tables present whole-brain activation maps and coordinate-based results. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of tobacco (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts, voxelwise whole-brain group analyses (flexible factorial Time x Stimulation interaction and one-sample t-test for smoking>neutral) with cluster-level correction and reported significant clusters (tables/figures). Methods state MRI field strength (1.5T) and processing software (SPM12); participant age range and sex/gender comparisons are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (image of a $100 bill) versus a control nonreward image in a within-subject design. The authors present whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation results (e.g., main effect of reward: reward > nonreward), with cluster-corrected maps and tables/figures. Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (money reward), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. Although the paper’s primary focus is nicotine administration, it includes a clear visual cue-reactivity contrast (reward > nonreward) suitable for a meta-analysis of visual reward cue-reactivity. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is available. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet exclusion criteria.

This study reports an fMRI task including visual alcohol cues (90 pictures of alcoholic and neutral beverages), uses within-subject contrasts between alcoholic vs non-alcoholic (control) stimuli at the individual level, and conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AFNI, 3dMVM) with family-wise error correction and reported clusters/coordinates (e.g., right amygdala, anterior cingulate). Necessary participant information (female subjects, ages 21–65), MRI scanner field strength (3T scanners), and processing software (AFNI) are reported. Whole-brain task-evoked maps and coordinate-based results are described in the text/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are violated. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli of natural rewards (foods containing chili). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (spicy food > non-spicy food), and group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with whole-brain FWE correction. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual/object cues (participants held and viewed a cigarette and control objects). The authors report within-participant contrasts comparing cigarette versus control cue exposure and present group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction; results are reported as tables of coordinates and figures. Participant demographics (male, age range and mean), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI, FSL, etc.) are all reported. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Hence all required inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is an fMRI study of visual drug (cocaine) and natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using backward-masked visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts (cocaine vs. neutral; sexual vs. neutral) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; statistical parametric t maps, cluster statistics and coordinates). Participant demographics (age, sex) are provided (22 male cocaine patients; mean age ~41), cue types (cocaine and sexual), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (SPM2) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward). It reports within-subject contrasts of high-hedonic food cues > control stimuli (H > U and U > O) and uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with correction for multiple comparisons. Relevant participant details (age range, sex distribution), cue type (food), scanner field (3.0 T), and processing software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This study is not an fMRI study and does not report any task-evoked whole-brain fMRI activation maps. It is an interventional tDCS study with behavioral and cognitive/subjective measures (appetite VAS, n-back task) in participants with obesity; no MRI data, no within-participant fMRI contrast of food cues>control, and no voxelwise whole-brain results. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (functional MRI study) and related requirements (I4, I5). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual food cues (natural reward) and includes within-participant contrasts (all food > non-food; high-calorie > low-calorie). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected whole-brain results) and details are provided in text, figures, and supplemental material. Participant demographics (male, ages 18–35), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all meta-analysis inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking cues with within-subject smoking cue>control contrasts, reporting participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner (3T) and processing software (SPM8). However, all voxel-wise statistics were restricted to an a priori ROI mask (i.e., ROI-restricted voxel-wise analysis) rather than reporting an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map. Thus it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results (I5) and falls under the exclusion criterion for studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results (E3). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual chocolate pictures vs neutral pictures, with within-subject contrasts (chocolate>neutral) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise regression analyses reported. The paper reports whole-brain results (cluster-corrected) with anatomical localisation and cluster coordinates, and provides participant sex (female undergraduates), cue type (food/chocolate), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual Pavlovian cues (black-and-white patterns) associated with food outcomes (natural rewards). It reports within-subject contrasts of food-outcome cues > no-outcome cues and other task-evoked contrasts, with group-level voxelwise statistical results reported as coordinates and thresholded clusters (including small-volume and exploratory whole-brain analyses). Relevant participant demographics, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are provided. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for fMRI cue-reactivity with visual stimuli, within-participant cue>control contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise results (reported in text/tables/coords), and requisite methodological details.

The study is an fMRI investigation using visual food cues (natural reward), with within-subject contrasts of food>nonfood. It reports group-level voxelwise analyses: GLM-derived activation maps and whole-brain parametric modulation/whole-brain regression results (FWE-corrected fusiform gyrus), not solely ROI results. Participant age/sex (young adult males), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This study is not an fMRI study and does not report any neuroimaging data or task-evoked whole-brain statistical maps. It is a behavioral/clinical pilot study assessing heroin craving with a visual analogue scale in methadone patients, with no fMRI methods, within-participant cue>control contrasts, or whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I7) and does not provide the required imaging data for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in adolescents. It uses within-subject contrasts (go vs no-go food trials and collapsed food cue activity versus baseline across sleep conditions), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (3dMVM) with peak coordinates and cluster results. Core participant information (age, sex distribution), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI, ANTs, SPSS) are all reported. Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and coordinates, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements for task-evoked maps. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

The study uses fMRI and visual smoking cues and reports behavioral cue pleasantness ratings, but the imaging results present whole-brain task maps only for an interoceptive attention task and resting-state/seed connectivity analyses. The paper does not report a within-participant, whole-brain contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (i.e., a cue-reactivity task activation map) required by the meta-analysis, so it fails inclusion criterion I4. Full text appears complete.

This study is not a task-based functional MRI (fMRI) study. It reports EEG/ERP (LORETA source estimates) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) tractography after tDCS, but no BOLD fMRI whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps of drug- or natural-reward cue reactivity. Therefore it fails the primary inclusion criteria requiring an fMRI study (I3) and a whole-brain task-evoked map (I5). While the paper does include within-participant cue contrasts (drug vs neutral) and reports participant/cue/MRI scanner details, the absence of fMRI whole-brain activation maps means it does not meet the review’s core requirements.

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue processing using visual stimuli and reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results with scanner and processing details, the reported fMRI analyses focus on contrasts between cognitive reappraisal instructions and an 'imagine eating' instruction for appetizing foods. The paper does not report a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., appetizing food > unappetizing food or food images > neutral/non-food images) in the provided full text. Because the meta-analysis requires at least one cue>control within-subject contrast, this study does not meet inclusion criterion I4 and thus must be excluded.

This study is not an fMRI cue-reactivity experiment. It reports behavioral, clinical, and self-report measures with factor analysis in an AUD sample; no task-based fMRI methods, no within-participant drug-or-reward-cue>control contrasts, and no whole-brain, voxelwise activation maps are described. Therefore it fails multiple inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I7) required for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion, so exclusion is based on content rather than incomplete reporting.

This is a task-based fMRI study of visual food cues (natural reward) with within-participant contrasts (food video epochs > control video epochs). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM2 with family-wise error correction and reporting of activation clusters (coordinates referenced in Table 2). Relevant participant details (sex, age range), cue type (food), MRI field strength (4T), and processing software (SPM2) are reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are violated.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of methamphetamine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). It reports a within-participant Methamphetamine Cue > Control Cue contrast and presents group-level whole-brain, voxelwise activation maps (cluster-corrected, Z>2.3, p<.05) with results described in text, figure, and table. Relevant methodological and sample details are provided (participant age/sex, cue type: methamphetamine, 3T scanner, processing software FSL). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (e-cigarette) cue-reactivity that used visual stimuli (images of e-cigarettes) and within-subject contrasts (sweet-, nicotine-, and sweet+nicotine-paired cues versus control). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (including exploratory whole-brain results and correlations that survived whole-brain correction) and also small-volume ROI tests; methods report participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine/e-cigarette), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM12). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of hedonic food cues > nonfood control stimuli, reported at the first-level and entered into group-level random-effects analyses. Whole-brain, voxelwise results are presented (statistical parametric maps and coordinate tables) with appropriate multiple comparison correction (cluster-level FDR), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Key methodological details are reported: participant age/sex summaries, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8). The paper reports full introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections (full text provided). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and includes within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts, the reported analyses are ROI-focused (a priori PCC ROI) and the main results are based on extracted PCC beta-weights. The only voxel-wise group analysis described was restricted to the PCC (i.e., not an unmasked whole-brain, group-level task activation map). Therefore the paper does not present a whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map as required. It thus meets the exclusion criterion for ROI-only reporting (E3) and cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This paper reports an fMRI cue-exposure study using visual drug-related vs. neutral pictures in a sample of adolescents with stimulant abuse. It includes a within-subject drug>neutral contrast, reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps (main effects and exploratory whole-brain analyses) and ROI analyses, and clearly provides participant age and sex, cue type (stimulants/cocaine/heroin), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM12). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an original human fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of smoking versus matched control (teeth-brushing) stimuli (e.g., BEGIN S2-T2, END S4-T4) at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise analyses implemented in SPM5, with results described in text and reported in tables (coordinates). Participant demographics (group sizes and sex) and scanner field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (SPM5) are reported. Thus it satisfies the review’s inclusion criteria for task-evoked, whole-brain fMRI cue-reactivity studies. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videos). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of smoking vs. non-smoking cues, provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME1, cluster-corrected maps), and includes figures/tables describing results and supplementary coordinate tables. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual presentation (participants viewed/held a cigarette via live video feed). The provided full text is a narrative/review article (theory and summary of neuroimaging findings) and contains only title, abstract, keywords, and metadata. It does not present original human fMRI methods, participants, experimental design, analyses, or results; no within-participant contrasts (e.g., drug-cues>control) or group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables are reported in the text provided. Therefore it is a non-empirical paper without original human fMRI data, meeting exclusion criterion E6. Additionally, the full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata present), so I cannot verify inclusion criteria I3–I7.

While this is an fMRI study using visual drug-related cues and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps (FSL/SPM, 3T scanner) and participant info, it does not present a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control (or natural reward > control) that represents standard cue-reactivity. The primary reported contrasts evaluate premature>correct responses within incentive contexts and interactions between premature responses across money vs drug conditions, rather than a simple drug‑cue > neutral cue contrast. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met, so the study cannot be included in a meta-analysis of cue‑reactivity contrasts.

This is an fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (explicit sexual images). It includes within-subject contrasts comparing sexual versus neutral pictures (Sex LO > Neutral LO; Sex PC > Neutral PC). Group-level second-level analyses were performed and the paper indicates whole-brain analyses are available in the supplementary material (coordinates/whole-brain results described). Participant age and sex, cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. Although ROI analyses are emphasized, whole-brain results are reported/available, so the study does not meet exclusion for ROI-only reporting. Therefore it meets all specified inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

This study does not meet the review's key inclusion requirement that cue-reactivity be assessed using visual stimuli (I3). The experimental manipulation used gustatory (taste) high-calorie cues delivered in the scanner (high-calorie drinks vs. water); although brief visual instructions accompanied delivery, the primary reward cues were tastes rather than visual stimuli. The study does satisfy several other inclusion criteria (within-subject contrast of high-calorie cues > control (water) (I4), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (I5), and reporting of whole-brain results in text/figures (I6)). Some required participant details are incomplete in the provided full text: age range is reported but sex distribution is not clearly provided in the excerpt, raising uncertainty about I7. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not use visual cue stimuli as required by the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual cues (pornographic pictures) to test cue-reactivity and their effect on task performance. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of explicit (pornographic) > neutral pictures and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM12) with whole-brain cluster-level FWE correction, and provides peak activations/tables and figures. Relevant participant information (male, age means), cue type (sexual), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. The explicitness (pornographic>neutral) main effect and interaction contrasts constitute appropriate task-evoked whole-brain maps matching the meta-analysis objective of natural reward (sexual) visual cue-reactivity.

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) using visual stimuli (I3 satisfied), the published analyses in this full text use an ROI approach and report ROI-based contrasts (e.g., Large PS > Small PS) rather than presenting group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps. The paper explicitly states the present study used an ROI approach and does not report whole-brain results for the contrasts relevant to cue-reactivity. Therefore it violates the review's requirement for whole-brain evidence and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses reported).

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) using visual stimuli and reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses, the group-level results presented are exclusively pre-post (surgery) difference maps (nogo_dessert_pre - nogo_dessert_post, nogo_vegetable_pre - nogo_vegetable_post). The study does not report an accompanying unmasked, group-level cue>control (e.g., food cues > control stimuli or food > neutral) whole-brain task activation map. The meta-analysis requires at least one within-participant cue>control group-level whole-brain map; reporting only time/difference contrasts without the main task effect meets exclusion criterion E5. Subject-level cue>rest contrasts were computed but not provided at the group level as the required cue>control effect for inclusion.

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts (hedonic > neutral foods; foods > non-food objects) and reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8), the study used an ROI-based analysis approach and explicitly notes that sample size was insufficient for whole-brain analysis. No unmasked, group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or whole-brain coordinate tables/figures are reported for the primary contrasts. This violates the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete.

The article is an fMRI event-related cue reactivity study using visual drug and food stimuli with within-subject contrasts (drug>neutral, food>neutral) and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses and AFNI preprocessing. Participant age and sex are reported. However, the full text provided does not report the MRI scanner field strength (e.g., 1.5T or 3T) in the main text; while supplementary materials are referenced, they were not provided here. Inclusion criterion I7 requires reporting of scanner field strength along with other methodological details. Because that required piece of information is not available in the provided full text, the study does not meet all inclusion criteria and must be excluded from the meta-analysis based on the information given.

Although this is an fMRI study that used visual cues to predict a natural reward (juice), the reported task analyses are based on region-of-interest (caudate and putamen) extracted activity measures and GWAS of those ROI values. The paper does not report a within-participant cue>control (or cue>neutral) contrast in the form needed for cue-reactivity meta-analysis, nor does it present group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or coordinate tables of whole-brain task effects. Therefore it fails the required whole-brain task-evoked evidence and effectively reports only ROI-based task results. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues (pictures) and neutral/evocative controls (meets cue modality). It reports within-participant contrasts (smoking vs. neutral) with observed increases in NAcc and amygdala activation in smokers. Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with cluster-correction and small-volume corrections; results are reported in text/tables and ROI analyses. Methods report participant demographics (age/gender distribution summarized), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0T) and processing software (AFNI). Therefore all required inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity whole-brain fMRI studies are satisfied.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing cigarette-predictive cues (CS+) versus control cues (CS−) (e.g., Attend CS+ vs Attend CS−) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (statistical maps reported at p<0.001). Participant age and sex (all male, ages reported), cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5 and FSL) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete for screening. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual monetary reward cues (ring of dollar signs) and neutral cues, with within-subject contrasts of reward vs. neutral trials. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (linear mixed effects on IRFs, cluster correction via AlphaSim) with reported peak coordinates and time courses. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (monetary reward), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (FSL, AFNI) are reported. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for natural reward cue-reactivity and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) visual cues and includes within-participant contrasts (fattening > non-fattening). However, the paper reports only ROI-based results (mean z-scores extracted from predefined ROIs) and does not present any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps, coordinates, or tables of whole-brain results. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual erotic (natural) and monetary cues. The full text describes within-subject contrasts of ‘erotic cue > control’ and ‘monetary cue > control’, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses reported (SPM2) and cluster- and voxel-level thresholds, coordinates, and figures/tables. Participant age and sex (heterosexual males, mean age reported), cue types (erotic, monetary), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM2) are all specified. The article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete for screening. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity and does not violate exclusion criteria.

The study used an fMRI alcohol cue paradigm with gustatory (taste) stimuli (alcohol taste vs. litchi juice), not visual cue stimuli. The meta-analysis requires cue-reactivity studies using visual stimuli (I3). Although the study meets other inclusion criteria (within-subject alcohol>control contrast, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, adequate reporting of participants, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software), it fails the essential visual-stimulus criterion and therefore must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine) and matched control images; participants (smokers and non-smokers) are described including age and sex balance. Within-subject contrasts comparing smoking versus control stimuli are reported (BEGIN/END contrasts, distraction and identification tasks). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using FSL/FLAME with FWE-corrected voxelwise thresholds and results reported with tables of coordinates and figures. Scanner field strength (1.5T) and processing software (FSL) are specified. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of food cue reactivity using visual stimuli with whole-brain analyses and appropriate reporting (age/sex, cue type = food, 3T scanner, SPM8). However, it does not include a within-participant contrast of food cues versus a non-food control (neutral) stimulus; all experimental conditions are food images (high vs low calorie, available vs unavailable). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 (no cue>control stimulus contrast). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6, I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) directly apply.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (a natural reward cue). The study reports within-participant contrasts of sexual videos > neutral and emotional control conditions and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM12 with second-level random-effects testing and multiple-comparison correction; coordinates and cluster results are provided in text/supplementary materials. Participant details (male participants, age inclusion 18–65), cue type (sexual), MRI field strength (3-T GE), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is an fMRI investigation of responses to food images (a natural reward) in adolescents, and reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie vs fixation). However, all reported statistical results are restricted to predefined ROIs (hippocampus, insula, thalamus, frontal regions) rather than an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Inclusion criterion I5 (presence of at least one whole-brain group-level task map) is not met; thus the study matches exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of food (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (package images) and within-participant contrasts comparing package types (regular vs healthier) and package/taste conditions. The study reports group-level voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain analyses followed by ROI masking) and provides cluster results and correlations; participant age/sex (34 healthy females, ages reported), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. Reporting includes whole-brain results (clusters/thresholds) and coordinates in text/supplement. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual sexual cues (a natural reward) with a within-participant contrast of sexual cues > neutral (and sex > other rewards). Group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM5) with peak coordinates, tables/figures and supplementary data described. Scanner field strength (3 T Philips Intera), processing software (SPM5), and participant characteristics including age/sex and sample sizes (12 PD hypersexuality, 12 PD controls) are reported. The paradigm and results satisfy all required reporting elements for inclusion in a meta-analysis of fMRI visual cue-reactivity for natural rewards.

This is an fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (food images) with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie vs. nonfood object; low-calorie vs. nonfood object) during premeal and postmeal states. Group-level voxelwise GLM results are reported, with whole-brain thresholds (p<.001, cluster >5, FDR corrected) and region-level results/coordinates and activation maps described in the text/figures. Cue type (food), MRI field strength (4.0T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. Participant sample size and BMI groupings are provided; a participant characteristics table is referenced (suggesting age/sex were reported in the full article). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 for the meta-analysis of visual reward cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI study of monetary incentive delay task using visual object cues and monetary gain/loss anticipation; it does not investigate cue-reactivity to drug cues (e.g., nicotine, alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, heroin) or natural reward-related cues specified by the review (e.g., food, sexual). Therefore it fails the key inclusion criterion I3. The manuscript does include within-participant contrasts (gain>neutral, loss>neutral) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results, coordinate tables/figures, participant age/sex, cue type (monetary), scanner (3T) and processing software (SPM8), so I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is an fMRI study (visual alcohol cues) with 61 adult nondependent drinkers. It includes a within-participant contrast of alcohol versus neutral cues, reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (voxel p<.001 with cluster p<.05 FWE) with coordinates/clusters provided, and reports processing software (SPM). Participant sex and cue type are described; imaging protocol details are available in the supplementary material. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity whole-brain fMRI studies and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (appetizing food images) with within-subject task contrasts versus baseline/ fixation and strategy contrasts (Close/Far). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (tables and cluster coordinates; AlphaSim correction), participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are all provided. The paper is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and reports whole-brain task activations suitable for inclusion in a cue-reactivity meta-analysis of natural rewards (food). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with group-level, whole-brain task analyses and adequate reporting of participants, scanner, and processing (satisfying I3, I5, I6, I7), it lacks a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control (neutral) stimuli as required by I4. The reported contrasts compare food images with and without calorie labels (CALORIES vs NO CALORIES) rather than food cues versus a neutral/non-reward control condition. No unmasked whole-brain cue>control contrast is described, so the study does not meet the essential I4 inclusion criterion for cue-reactivity meta-analysis. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical within-subject, double-blind placebo-controlled fMRI study using visual erotic (sexual) scenes as natural reward cues and neutral control stimuli. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (erotic > neutral, fearful > neutral, erotic > fearful) and group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected results (and supplementary uncorrected maps), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Participant age and sex (55 healthy young males, mean age reported), cue type (sexual/erotic), scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Thus it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (written labels and cue images). The authors report within-subject contrasts comparing labeled beverage cues (low-calorie, high-calorie, neutral) including high>low, low>high, and comparisons versus neutral. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results (SPM8) with cluster-level FWE correction reported; details on participants (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software are provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Although the article examines neural responses related to food cues and reports behavioral craving ratings to visual food stimuli, the fMRI data are resting-state seed-based functional connectivity analyses (no task fMRI cue-reactivity scan). There is no within-participant task contrast of food cues > control stimuli and no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported. Therefore the study does not meet I3, I4, or I5 and directly meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only seed-based/resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts (food > non-food; high-calorie > low-calorie). The authors report group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (voxelwise) with cluster-correction and describe significant clusters, and also provide ROI analyses. Relevant methodological details are reported: participant age range, mention of sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (penile-vaginal penetration) relevant to natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity. The manuscript reports within-subject contrasts of sexual cues versus control stimuli (e.g., PEN>BOD, PEN>NEU). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (SPM8; FWE-corrected maps and conjunction analyses; figures of whole-brain results are provided). Relevant participant and scanner details are reported (female participants with ages, 3T Philips scanner, SPM8 preprocessing). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual cues (natural reward) and neutral controls. The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing sexual > neutral backgrounds (task-based cue-reactivity), performed whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses using SPM12 with FDR-corrected results and reported activation tables/figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software are all reported. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This is an fMRI study using visual erotic pictures (sexual natural rewards) in a within-subject, randomized, placebo-controlled crossover design. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., placebo erotic > placebo neutral; GHB neutral > placebo neutral) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain threshold p<.001 reported), with ROI analyses supplementary. Participant age/sex, cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports task activation maps).

This is an empirical fMRI study in adolescents assessing neural responsivity to natural reward-related visual cues (Coca-Cola product and logo advertisements) and includes within-subject contrasts of reward-related cues > non-food control ads (Coke product ads > non-food ads; Coke logo ads > non-food ads). Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-level FWE correction; coordinates/tables and figures provided). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (food/soft drink), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8, AFNI). The full-text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

Full text appears incomplete: only references and article metadata are provided (no introduction, methods, results, or discussion). Because core article content is missing, I cannot verify whether this is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli, whether it reports within-participant cues>control whole-brain contrasts, or whether participant/cue/scanner/processing details are reported (I3–I7). Therefore the study cannot be assessed against the inclusion criteria and is excluded pending receipt of the complete full text.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (milkshake vs tasteless solution images). It includes within-subject contrasts of unpaired milkshake cue > unpaired tasteless cue, and group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM5) with reported peak coordinates and statistical maps (with small-volume corrections reported). Key methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, SPM5 processing). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without whole-brain task maps, or non-empirical) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity using visual natural reward stimuli.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (food) in human participants. It presents within-subject contrasts of food>control (HC–C, LC–C, HC–LC, Food–C) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with cluster-wise inference and reported clusters/coordinates. Relevant participant and imaging details are reported (female participants with PCOS, scanner 3.0T Siemens, processing with SPM8; cue type = food). Results include whole-brain task-evoked maps and covariate analyses (insulin sensitivity, BMI). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so is complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of food cues > nonfood control stimuli, reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked analyses (whole-brain results described and illustrated), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM-12). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This study investigates maternal neural responses to infant faces and cries (social/parental cues), not drug cues or the natural reward types targeted in the review (e.g., food or sexual cues). It therefore does not satisfy key inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli of the specified types) or I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli). The full text is complete and does report whole-brain voxelwise analyses (satisfying I5), reports whole-brain results in the text/tables (I6), and provides participant/scanner/processing details (I7). Because I3 and I4 are not met, the study must be excluded.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual natural (sexual) reward cues and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task results (tables/figures), it does not present a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., erotic cues > neutral/control) or an equivalent unmasked task activation map required by I4. The analyses focus on parametric modulation of subjective value, delay-related effects, and group×medication interactions rather than a simple cue>control contrast. Additionally, the full text does not clearly report MRI scanner field strength (required by I7). Therefore not all required inclusion criteria (I4 and I7) are met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (fMRI with visual natural reward cues), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I6 (results reported in tables/figures). Exclusion criterion applicable: E5 (no accompanying unmasked, within-participant cue>control whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study of food (natural reward) cues meets multiple inclusion criteria: it uses visual food stimuli (I3), reports within-participant contrasts (highly desirable>less desirable; food>non-food) (I4), and reports group-level second-level voxelwise statistics with coordinate-level results and SVC-corrected peaks (I5,I6). However, it does not report essential participant age information or explicitly state the primary processing software used (only indirect mention of marsbar), so it fails inclusion criterion I7 requiring relevant info on participant age, sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) in children. The design includes within-participant conditions (high-calorie, low-calorie, and blurred control images) and models blurred images as an implicit baseline, allowing contrasts of food cues > control. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (ANOVA with cluster correction) and significant clusters are reported (figures/tables). The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3.0T), and processing software (AFNI). Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine) with within-participant contrasts (craving vs neutral and regulation vs craving). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM8 with cluster-level correction and coordinates reported; results are presented in text, figures, and tables. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software are reported. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation of visual food cues with within-subject contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM results (figures/tables with coordinates), scanner field strength (3 T), processing software (SPM5), and participant sex (two women, one man). However, the provided full text does not report participant ages, so criterion I7 (relevant information reported regarding participant age and sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software) is not fully satisfied. Because all inclusion criteria must be met and I7 is not fulfilled in the provided full text, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).
